item.title: 'Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': World Cup-winner sends strong message on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
item.description: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances. But his stunning innings against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars could well be the most special of them all. The youngster went after the bowlers from the start and completely dominated the opposition attack. Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus. Many former cricketers and experts have backed the youngster for a regular place in India's T20I team. However, his latest knock also underlined his ability to make an impact in the 50-over format. Former India captain and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth feels the team management must take bold decisions to give Sooryavanshi a bigger role in Indian cricket. Srikkanth questions Gambhir's approach Sooryavanshi has featured in 10 T20Is for India but is yet to cement his place in the playing XI. With the full-strength team available, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been preferred as openers. Srikkanth feels the youngster is not getting enough opportunities despite his impressive performances. He also had a strong message for India head coach Gautam Gambhir. "We need to make some strong moves. Vaibhav was made Bihar captain right away. He was the vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy; him and Ishan (Kishan) won the title. He has been promoted to that level. Gautam is just keeping deaf ears," Srikkanth said, speaking on his YouTube channel. "The team management is playing one game, saying he has to be groomed, and not giving him chances. This guy, on the other hand, is playing his own game. You say it is not in your hands and all of that. Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting. No one can hit like this. Just look at this," he added. 'This is another level' Srikkanth was left stunned by the variety of shots Sooryavanshi played during his remarkable innings. He also praised the youngster's power and timing, saying he had rarely seen anything like it. "What is this? Have you seen anyone hitting the ball like this? Look at the shots he has played. He has his shots everywhere in all ranges. This is another level. This does not happen in book cricket either. I have never seen these kinds of shots. Who is this guy? Which generation is he from? Where does he get so much power and sense of timing?" he further said. Srikkanth also compared the 15-year-old's batting to that of some of the biggest hitters in the game, including AB de Villiers and Chris Gayle. "I have not seen anyone playing like this in a team. Even (AB) De Villiers and (Chris) Gayle did not play like this," Srikkanth concluded. 136184442

item.title: Botham back as Morgan-Williams to make first start
item.description: James Botham and Reuben Morgan-Williams were part of the Wales squad that beat New Zealand [Getty Images/Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales flanker James Botham has been recalled by head coach Steve Tandy as one of five changes for the Nations Championship finale against Japan at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. In the only backline alteration for the game in Twickenham, Ospreys scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams will make his first Wales start, with Tomos Williams named among the replacements. Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins will captain the side for the first time in more than two years with regular skipper Dewi Lake and flanker Jac Morgan also dropping to the bench. Prop Rhys Carre and hooker Ryan Elias make their first starts of the November campaign, while lock Adam Beard returns at the expense of Ben Carter. Wales have named an experienced bench that includes 294 caps. Botham back after missing Australia Botham produced a player-of-the-match display in the 35-28 victory against New Zealand after making 30 tackles but was left out of the 29-26 defeat by Australia in favour of Cardiff colleague Alex Mann. It was a decision which Botham’s father Liam, himself a former Cardiff wing, said Tandy had got wrong. “I know there's a lot been spoken about it,” said Tandy. “Everyone has got their opinions and people generally tell you who should be in the team and they never tell you who shouldn't. “We're a tight group and as a coach I make sure I speak to all the players before if they are not selected. There'll be reasons why, whether it be bigger picture or whether it is form. “I'll always speak to those, that's a special thing and the connection we feel in our environment.” Botham, who became a father earlier this week, will play at open-side flanker against Japan after starring at blind-side against the All Blacks, with Mann and number eight Aaron Wainwright completing the back row. “James was outstanding against the All Blacks, but we've got a back row depth there that we can move things around and freshen things up," said Tandy. “James has had his little one, he's coming back in full of energy. We were so pleased for him things have gone well there." Wales need strong finish to campaign - Morgan A world-class winger - Louis Rees-Zammit 2.0 Chance for Morgan-Williams to shine at nine Ospreys number nine Morgan-Williams is preparing for his first start in a position that has been dominated by Saracens scrum-half Williams during the Tandy era. Williams has started 14 out of the 15 internationals, including the previous 11, with opportunities in short supply for others. But Williams came off early in the second half against Australia with a groin problem. Carre, named Welsh rugby writers player of the 2025-26 season, is given his first start this autumn, with Nicky Smith dropping out of the squad. Saracens loose-head Carre missed the first month of the season because of a hamstring injury and his only appearance of the autumn Tests so far was off the bench agains

There'll be reasons why, whether it be bigger picture or whether it is form. “I'll always speak to those, that's a special thing and the connection we feel in our environment.” Botham, who became a father earlier this week, will play at open-side flanker against Japan after starring at blind-side against the All Blacks, with Mann and number eight Aaron Wainwright completing the back row. “James was outstanding against the All Blacks, but we've got a back row depth there that we can move things around and freshen things up," said Tandy. “James has had his little one, he's coming back in full of energy. We were so pleased for him things have gone well there." Wales need strong finish to campaign - Morgan A world-class winger - Louis Rees-Zammit 2.0 Chance for Morgan-Williams to shine at nine Ospreys number nine Morgan-Williams is preparing for his first start in a position that has been dominated by Saracens scrum-half Williams during the Tandy era. Williams has started 14 out of the 15 internationals, including the previous 11, with opportunities in short supply for others. But Williams came off early in the second half against Australia with a groin problem. Carre, named Welsh rugby writers player of the 2025-26 season, is given his first start this autumn, with Nicky Smith dropping out of the squad. Saracens loose-head Carre missed the first month of the season because of a hamstring injury and his only appearance of the autumn Tests so far was off the bench against Japan. Elias, a replacement in the three previous November internationals, is handed his first Test start since the 2024 Six Nations match against France. Montpellier lock Beard returns after missing the loss to Australia after suffering a shoulder injury against New Zealand. Scarlets wing Ellis Mee is given his first involvement in the campaign after being named as a replacement. Tandy has settled on his backline with full-back Blair Murray, wing Louis Rees-Zammit, centres Eddie James and Max Llewellyn and fly-half Sam Costelow starting all four matches in the November campaign as well as prop Archie Griffin and Jenkins. Uncapped quartet Che Hope, Macs Page, Rhys Barratt and Aneurin Owen are among the players who will not be given game time. Wales have won three and lost three of their six Nations Championship matches to finish fifth in the northern hemisphere group, a position matched by Japan in the southern hemisphere section. Wales will face Eddie Jones’ Japan side for a fifth time inside two years with Wales winning three out of the four games. It is the first match of a Saturday double-header, with England and New Zealand to follow. “We were frustrated and disappointed with losing last weekend,” said Tandy. “We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been but there were a lot of positives in the performance to take also. “We want to go out there, be ruthless and show improvement on our previous performance against Japan." How they line up Wales: Murray: Rees-Zammit, E James, Llewellyn, Adams: Costelow, Morgan-Williams; Carre, Elias, Griffin, D Jenkins (capt), Beard, Mann, Botham, Wainwright. Replacements: Lake, G Thomas, Lewis, Plumtree, J Morgan, Tomos Williams, Hawkins, Mee. Japan: TBC Replacements: TBC Referee: Luke Pearce (England) Assistant Referees: Matthew Carley (England) & Damian Schneider (Argentina) TMO: Ian Tempest (England) FPRO: Matteo Liperini (Italy).

item.title: Bearman to continue with Haas in 2027
item.description: In 2025, Oliver Bearman outscored his team-mate Estaban Ocon by three points. This season, he scored three times the points of Ocon before the Frenchman was dropped during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend [Getty Images] Britain's Oliver Bearman will continue to race for the Haas team in Formula 1 in 2027. The US-based team announced the 21-year-old's new deal on Thursday, at the start of the Qatar Grand Prix weekend. It marks Bearman's third full season with Haas, for whom he first raced for two one-off events in 2024 before becoming a full-time driver in 2025. The announcement ends a protracted negotiation period in which Bearman's management were seeking reassurances about his future from Ferrari. Bearman is a member of the Italian team's driver academy and has ambitions to race for Ferrari in the future. It was not immediately clear what reassurances Bearman had been given about his future by Ferrari. Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A Camara to continue with Haas for final two races Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us. "We've seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. "He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward." Bearman added: "It's no secret that I'm delighted to be continuing with Haas into 2027. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I've felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. "We've got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I'm excited to lead that work, building on what we've achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business." Bearman will be partnered at Haas next season with Brazilian Rafael Camara, who is also a member of the Ferrari driver academy. Camara has started racing for Haas at the end of this season, following the team's sacking of Frenchman Esteban Ocon midway through the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend. Bearman's concerns about his future had been rooted in the fact that there might not be a seat available at Ferrari for some considerable time. Charles Leclerc is on a long-term contract there, and while Lewis Hamilton's deal is believed to end after 2027, the seven-time champion is keen to continue in F1 for a number more years. Bearman, who said at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, that he was "quite disappointed" his new contract had not yet been sorted so late in the season, is believed to have been exploring his options. His management is said to have been asking Ferrari for reassurances about his future, either about the possibility of racing for the main team, or if that is not an option, being allowed to pursue a career at a more competitive team than Haas. How to follow Qatar Grand Prix on the BBC Andrew Benson Q&A: Send us your questions Listen to Chequered Flag on BBC

item.title: 51 Years Later, One of Peanuts’ Best Sally Brown Strips Is Still a Perfect School Joke
item.description: For years, one of the problems with reading Charles Schulz's Peanuts was the inconsistency among its collected editions . You'd think that Peanuts’ publishers, as the stewards of one of the most influential comic strips in the Western world, would simply reprint the comics in chronological order. It was rarely that simple.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch

item.title: UK Home Office waved through border system without a working fix for bad data
item.description: The Information Commission's Office (ICO) has reprimanded the UK Home Office over a border watchlist system launched without an effective way to correct inaccurate personal information. The regulator said the failings risked people being wrongly detained for additional checks at the UK border, potentially causing distress and other harm. The platform in question, Helios, was slated to replace its predecessor, Warnings Index, in September 2024 and despite an initial delay due to concerns over data quality, went live the following month. Both Helios and Warnings Index are watch-listing systems, designed to allow law enforcement officials – mainly but not exclusively Border Force – to check people's data against official records at the UK border. Helios's federated operating model, whereby the data sources are not centrally managed, yielded quicker results than Warnings Index, but contained a critical flaw in that operational staff could not alter incorrect records. Platform operators, such as Border Force officers, could not amend the data that feeds into it, neither after the fact nor in real time. This was not the case with Warnings Index, which had a dedicated team responsible for correcting data entries in real time. Under Helios, staff were supposed to report inaccuracies to the organization responsible for the relevant source data, which would make the correction. One slight problem: there was no established reporting system at the time Helios was launched on October 2. The platform went live anyway, as officials deemed the data integrity and security risks presented by Warnings Index to be greater than those of Helios. Just nine days passed before the Home Office's data protection officer had to submit a breach report after Helios operational staff said they didn't know how to request data corrections. During the time, Helios operators sent 87 data rectification requests to the Warnings Index correction team, despite it having no capability to make the required changes to the data. The Home Office later said that many other requests likely weren't logged as the proper processes were not in place, and that staff should have logged the issue through a ServiceNow IT ticket, as any other departmental civil servant with any kind of IT issue would have. But the Home Office also said that including personal data in those helpdesk tickets would itself constitute a data breach. The ICO said in its reprimand document [PDF] that it is "unclear" how such a reporting arrangement could realistically work in practice, given that a report would require details from a subject's record that required rectification as well as the new, accurate information that should be used to replace it. The Home Office's proposed workaround was to get operational staff to verbally read out said personal data over a phone call with the IT helpdesk – a procedure it described as possible "but cumbersome." item.dc:creator: Connor Jones
item.content:encoded: The Information Commission's Office (ICO) has reprimanded the UK Home Office over a border watchlist system launched without an effective way to correct inaccurate personal information. The regulator said the failings risked people being wrongly detained for additional checks at the UK border, potentially causing distress and other harm. The platform in question, Helios, was slated to replace its predecessor, Warnings Index, in September 2024 and despite an initial delay due to concerns over data quality, went live the following month. Both Helios and Warnings Index are watch-listing systems, designed to allow law enforcement officials – mainly but not exclusively Border Force – to check people's data against official records at the UK border. Helios's federated operating model, whereby the data sources are not centrally managed, yielded quicker results than Warnings Index, but contained a critical flaw in that operational staff could not alter incorrect records. Platform operators, such as Border Force officers, could not amend the data that feeds into it, neither after the fact nor in real time. This was not the case with Warnings Index, which had a dedicated team responsible for correcting data entries in real time. Under Helios, staff were supposed to report inaccuracies to the organization responsible for the relevant source data, which would make the correction. One slight problem: there was no established reporting system at the time Helios was launched on October 2. The platform went live anyway, as officials deemed the data integrity and security risks presented by Warnings Index to be greater than those of Helios. Just nine days passed before the Home Office's data protection officer had to submit a breach report after Helios operational staff said they didn't know how to request data corrections. During the time, Helios operators sent 87 data rectification requests to the Warnings Index correction team, despite it having no capability to make the required changes to the data. The Home Office later said that many other requests likely weren't logged as the proper processes were not in place, and that staff should have logged the issue through a ServiceNow IT ticket, as any other departmental civil servant with any kind of IT issue would have. But the Home Office also said that including personal data in those helpdesk tickets would itself constitute a data breach. The ICO said in its reprimand document [PDF] that it is "unclear" how such a reporting arrangement could realistically work in practice, given that a report would require details from a subject's record that required rectification as well as the new, accurate information that should be used to replace it. The Home Office's proposed workaround was to get operational staff to verbally read out said personal data over a phone call with the IT helpdesk – a procedure it described as possible "but cumbersome." It took the Home Office more than a year to implement a temporary data-rectification method, which involved a BX Data Query tile on the IT Now platform, allowing Helios operators to securely report data accuracy issues. The new method went live on October 25, 2025. By March 18, 2026, the Home Office said the new process had received more than 6,500 correction requests and around 5,000 records had been removed. The ICO said it "remains concerned" about the efficacy of this method, given that operators cannot include personal data in the tile report, but the regulator is satisfied the problem is at least in part fixed. The Home Office also said it was aware of an increase in customer complaints following Helios's launch, and around 800 cases in which people were delayed at the UK border pending additional checks. It was unable to attribute a specific number of these to Helios's technical issues, however. "The Home Office further stated that it was not aware of any data subjects suffering distress as a result of using its services at the UK border," the ICO's report stated. The Home Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "People must be able to trust that decisions about their immigration status at the UK border are made with accurate, up to date information," said Joanne Stones, investigations manager at the ICO. "They also have the right to expect that when information is inaccurate, there is a swift and efficient way for it to be corrected." She added: "We recognise that federated systems like Helios present unique challenges and welcome the steps the Home Office has taken since this issue was identified. However, the Home Office must ensure that its permanent solution provides a robust and effective way to identify and correct inaccurate information without delay." The ICO's public sector enforcement policy favors guidance, reprimands, and other interventions, reserving fines for the most egregious cases. Its rationale is to avoid diverting money from public services and effectively punishing those affected twice. Fines have included £350,000 for a 2021 MoD email that exposed details of Afghan evacuation applicants , and £750,000 for the PSNI's 2023 disclosure of workforce information , including surnames, initials, ranks, and roles. The PSNI penalty was reduced from £5.6 million under the public sector approach. ®

item.title: Schalke 04’s Loris Karius plays coy on Bayern Munich transfer links
item.description: Photo by Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images | Getty Images Loris Karius’s career hit a downward spiral following his 2017/18 Champions League Final mishap with Liverpool. After losing confidence, he had a two-year loan spell at Beşiktaş, followed by stints at Union Berlin, Newcastle United, and a return to Liverpool. Eventually, Karius landed at 2. Bundesliga side Schalke 04, where he rebuilt his confidence. Last season, he helped Die Königsblauen capture the 2. Bundesliga title and earn promotion back to Germany’s top flight for the first time since the 2022/23 season. Now, the German shot-stopper is putting together a strong campaign with Schalke—and has caught Bayern Munich’s attention. The rumors linking Karius to Bavaria caught many off guard, including the goalkeeper himself. “I heard about it just like you did,” Karius said (as reported by @iMiaSanMia ). “It’s not my place to comment on rumors, and this isn’t the right occasion for that either. I haven’t spoken to anyone. My day-to-day work here is demanding enough as it is. I feel very comfortable at Schalke and really enjoy playing here. We have a lot to look forward to in the coming weeks, so my full focus is on that.” Karius m ay not know much about Bayern’s interest right now, though he’ll have plenty to think about if Die Rekordmeister decides he’s the right veteran option to back up Jonas Urbig next season. item.title: Cristian Chivu praises Inter's mentality after crucial Champions League victory over Stuttgart
item.description: FBL-C1-EUR-FEYENOORD-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter Milan manager Cristian Chivu has praised his side's defensive discipline and mental resilience following their crucial 2-0 victory over VfB Stuttgart at San Siro. The Nerazzurri secured the three points through a Petar Sucic penalty and a late strike from Lautaro Martinez to move up the Champions League table. Nerazzurri find defensive resolve at San Siro Inter successfully navigated a high-pressure European night on Wednesday, securing a win against Stuttgart that alleviates the sting of their recent domestic struggles. After suffering through a chaotic 4-4 draw with Atalanta in which they squandered a two-goal lead, the Italian giants knew they needed a clinical performance to leapfrog their German opponents in the league phase standings. The breakthrough arrived via a penalty converted by Petar Sucic following a handball, before Lautaro Martinez emerged from the bench to seal the victory. While the performance wasn't always fluid, the ability to grind out a result against a dangerous Stuttgart outfit suggests the squad has learned from their recent defensive lapses. "We relied on mentality, organisation, intensity, accepting that Champions League games are not easy, that you cannot dominate them from start to finish,” the Inter boss explained to Sky Sport Italia . He acknowledged that the team had to be patient, adding: "At times you need to stay in the match, try to make the most of opposition errors, but also try to be proactive when possible. The moments of a match are important and you need to read them." Chivu defends tactical adjustments Despite the win, questions remain regarding Inter's tendency to drop their intensity during certain phases of play. Chivu addressed these concerns by pointing out that his team was prepared to suffer when Stuttgart pushed forward early on. The manager felt his side successfully weathered an opening storm before growing into the contest, noting that they could have even been ahead by the interval if they had shown more clinical finishing in the final third. "We did well not to get swayed by their intensity in the first 20 minutes, so we accepted that we had to defend a bit deeper, but still with energy and pressing them on the ball. We did well to defend the crosses, as we knew they would be dangerous down the wings," Chivu noted. item.content:encoded: FBL-C1-EUR-FEYENOORD-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter Milan manager Cristian Chivu has praised his side's defensive discipline and mental resilience following their crucial 2-0 victory over VfB Stuttgart at San Siro. The Nerazzurri secured the three points through a Petar Sucic penalty and a late strike from Lautaro Martinez to move up the Champions League table. Nerazzurri find defensive resolve at San Siro Inter successfully navigated a high-pressure European night on Wednesday, securing a win against Stuttgart that alleviates the sting of their recent domestic struggles. After suffering through a chaotic 4-4 draw with Atalanta in which they squandered a two-goal lead, the Italian giants knew they needed a clinical performance to leapfrog their German opponents in the league phase standings. The breakthrough arrived via a penalty converted by Petar Sucic following a handball, before Lautaro Martinez emerged from the bench to seal the victory. While the performance wasn't always fluid, the ability to grind out a result against a dangerous Stuttgart outfit suggests the squad has learned from their recent defensive lapses. "We relied on mentality, organisation, intensity, accepting that Champions League games are not easy, that you cannot dominate them from start to finish,” the Inter boss explained to Sky Sport Italia . He acknowledged that the team had to be patient, adding: "At times you need to stay in the match, try to make the most of opposition errors, but also try to be proactive when possible. The moments of a match are important and you need to read them." Chivu defends tactical adjustments Despite the win, questions remain regarding Inter's tendency to drop their intensity during certain phases of play. Chivu addressed these concerns by pointing out that his team was prepared to suffer when Stuttgart pushed forward early on. The manager felt his side successfully weathered an opening storm before growing into the contest, noting that they could have even been ahead by the interval if they had shown more clinical finishing in the final third. "We did well not to get swayed by their intensity in the first 20 minutes, so we accepted that we had to defend a bit deeper, but still with energy and pressing them on the ball. We did well to defend the crosses, as we knew they would be dangerous down the wings," Chivu noted. Analysing the Atalanta fallout The shadow of the recent 4-4 draw against Atalanta loomed large over the pre-match build-up, but Chivu was adamant that he did not need to overhaul his approach despite the late collapse in Bergamo. Instead, he focused on fine-tuning the mental aspects of the game. He stressed that a coach must provide the right motivation for every individual fixture, ensuring that the squad remains unified even when results or performances are not perfect. "There always need to be interventions, when things go well or badly. We made a clear analysis of that match, because for around 75-80 minutes we played well, we lacked something in the final 10 minutes, but that doesn’t mean throwing away all the good things that were done that night,” Chivu said. Unity powers European turnaround The triumph extends Inter's winning streak in the Champions League to three straight matches, completely transforming the mood around a campaign that opened with back-to-back defeats against Real Madrid and Club Brugge. Even amid lingering questions over occasional dips in focus, Chivu made it clear that collective spirit remains non-negotiable. "The job of a coach is to transmit the right motivation in every match. It's not always easy to maintain the same level, sometimes we do it better than others, but the important thing is that the team remains united and nobody starts pointing the finger at anyone else. We cannot always be perfect, but what we must never lack is the right attitude and mentality. We saw that tonight, and it is no coincidence that we brought home the victory," he concluded.

item.title: Viktor Gyokeres warns Arsenal not to ‘waste energy’ on Man City sanctions as Gunners eye back-to-back titles
item.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Viktor Gyokeres has issued a firm rallying cry to his Arsenal teammates, insisting the club will not waste a single second of focus on Manchester City’s ongoing legal battles. The Swedish international is determined to secure consecutive Premier League titles and believes the Gunners are now fully accustomed to the pressure of being frontrunners. Arsenal host struggling City amid legal uncertainty Emirates Stadium hosts a pivotal Premier League showdown on Sunday as Arsenal face Manchester City for the first time since September's financial regulations verdict. City were found guilty of serious breaches but have lodged an appeal , leaving potential sanctions unresolved and the title race in limbo. Since that ruling, Enzo Maresca's side have suffered a sharp slump. They have claimed just one victory across their last seven matches in all competitions, collecting a single point from a possible 12 in the league. Gyokeres dismisses off-pitch noise and respects City's quality Asked whether potential sanctions against City could alter the title race, Gyokeres brushed off the off-field drama: "No. It is what it is. We are focused on the game on Sunday. We can't control that. It has nothing to do with us. So, we don't put any energy into that." Despite City's poor run of form, the Sweden international warned against underestimating Sunday's visitors. "They still have a very good squad and very good players," Gyokeres continued. "Sometimes, you may have a period where you don't get the results all the time - which is normal for any club. It is going to be a difficult game on Sunday. But it is always fun with big games. It is going to be good." Arteta's champions chase historic consecutive crowns Mikel Arteta's side sit six points clear of last season's runners-up as clear favourites to retain the Premier League crown for the first time in Arsenal's history. Fresh from scoring in Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund , Gyokeres is pushing to start and emphasised their title hunger. "We always want to win titles and we know how tough it is in the Premier League with the games and the teams," he said. "But we have an amazing squad, amazing players, so that's the aim. We push each other every day to achieve that and we are definitely going to go for it. "We always go into games wanting to win, and overall we have done well this season. Last season, we were on top of the league for most of the time. We are used to that position now and the main goal is to keep it that way and to win on Sunday." High-stakes Emirates showdown shapes the title race Sunday's clash gives Arsenal a prime chance to tighten their grip on top spot and pile further pressure on their faltering rivals. item.title: Fury vs Joshua: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight
item.description: This December, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally clash in arguably the biggest fight in British boxing history. The two former world heavyweight champions will headline in Cardiff, with more than 70,000 fans expected to watch as “AJ” and the “Gypsy King” settle a longstanding grudge. The pair have been linked for the best part of a decade, and even with their unbeaten records and titles deserting them, interest in Fury vs Joshua has never fully waned – although perhaps the bout would’ve been better five years ago . Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua in September (PA Wire) Still, the pair will finally square off at long last, with the vacant WBA “Super” belt on the line, though bragging rights are the true prize here. Here’s all you need to know: When is the fight? Fury vs Joshua will take place on Friday 11 December. Per a Cardiff Council meeting on 25 November , main-event ring walks will begin at 1am GMT on Saturday (5pm PT / 7pm CT / 8pm ET on Friday). Therefore, the preceding main card could begin any time from 9pm GMT (1pm PT / 3pm CT / 4pm ET). The late start is to ensure a greater US audience. How can I watch it? The event will stream live exclusively on Netflix worldwide. It will be not be a standalone pay-per-view event, meaning it will be available to all Netflix subscribers. Odds Fury – 4/7 Joshua – 16/1 Draw – 13/8 Fury and Joshua’s fight will stream live on Netflix (Getty) Via Betway , correct as of 23/11/26. Get all the latest boxing betting sites’ offers. The Independent vets betting sites for usability, security and responsible gambling tools. You can claim free bets here to use across a range of sports. Please read the terms. Tale of the tape: What is each man’s record, height, reach and age? Fury will enter the fight with a 36-2-1 record as a professional, including 25 KO wins. His sole losses were points defeats by Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, following his controversial draw with Deontay Wilder in 2018. The 38-year-old stands at 6ft 9in (although this has been seen as exaggerated throughout his career!) and has a reach of 85in. Meanwhile, Joshua is 30-4 as a pro with 27 KO wins, having lost to Andy Ruiz Jr and Daniel Dubois via stoppage and Usyk on points twice. AJ, 37 years old, is 6ft 6in tall with a reach of 82in. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino ‘so proud’ of Man Utd players despite schoolboy errors against Sporting CP
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino was proud of Manchester United’s performance and his players’ early progress in the action-packed 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League. The former Argentina international began his reign with a chastening 4-0 loss at rivals Liverpool on Sunday, when Leny Yoro’s early – and subsequently overturned – red card was the catalyst for Anfield agony. More frustration followed on Wednesday, when Senne Lammens gifted Sporting a penalty converted by Luis Suarez shortly after denying him from the spot before Bruno Fernandes ’ double with the help of a bobble put United in front. But Suarez would level in the second half after nudging Lammens when attempting to gather a high ball and Pochettino’s hopes of a first win ended when home goalkeeper Kaique Pereira’s own goal was ruled out. United saw a late winner controversially ruled out (Zed Jameson/PA) Szymon Marciniak adjudged Patrick Dorgu to have fouled him having been sent to the monitor on a night when the referee’s early whistle meant a disallowed first half Amad Diallo goal could not be overturned. Youri Tielemans was incorrectly booked for his role in that incident and picked up a second booking at the end of an eventful night that saw Pochettino focus on the positives in Portugal . “I am so proud of our players, my players,” Pochettino told TNT Sports. “It was a really tough game. “I like the team during 90 minutes, the personality, the character. And it’s true that it’s difficult to find some game that (you will) be more punished. “We were punished a lot in different actions that were key, but I think everyone that watched the game saw all the action. “Only what I can say is I feel proud about the players. I think we today showed the way that we want to play. It’s only one week working together. I feel so proud. I told them after the game.” Referee Marciniak’s poor performance will dominate the fallout to the draw at the Estadio Jose Alvalade, as will goalkeeper Lammens’ latest shaky display in a season replete with individual errors by United players. “Always we need to do double effort,” Pochettino said. “We need to concentrate more and focus more and try to (do) recovery better, do all the effort. Senne Lammens produced a poor performance in Portugal (Zed Jameson/PA) “I think in this type of situation we start to fix also with results, but with (a) performance like today that is for me is the best medicine to prepare the next game.” Pochettino’s frantic start to life in charge continues on Saturday afternoon at Old Trafford, where he will take charge of United for the first time against Brentford. The embattled Red Devils have just one win to show from their opening 11 Premier League matches and languish 19th in the standings. “I think we need to encourage and we need to really believe in our play,” Pochettino added. “We need to believe more and more and more. “I think we need to give the capacity and the tools to perform and of course improving things. “But that

item.title: US targets Africa’s critical minerals to counter rivals
item.description: In 2026, the United States went on an economic offensive looking to access critical minerals across Africa in its race to compete with China for materials that are essential for new technologies and the energy transformation. Will 2027 deliver on these promises for African governments and will the new Democrat-controlled US Congress complicate US deals with investigations into their transparency? – Investments or promises? – American companies and consortiums this year announced large-scale mining investment projects through partnerships in Guinea, South Africa, Mozambique and Kenya. But it was the strategic partnership agreed in December 2025 with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) that illustrated Washington’s economic push to secure its supply of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China. China has had a long head-start. It began investing in the African mining sector in the 1990s. The deal stipulated that Kinshasa would identify a portfolio of mining assets on which American investors have a right of first offer. In return, the Congolese government secured diplomatic support from Washington on security in its volatile eastern region, rocked by violence by myriad armed groups for more than 30 years. Since then, the American company Virtus Minerals, in partnership with the Indian group Lloyds Metals&Energy, has announced the acquisition of Chemaf, a heavily indebted Congolese company specialising in copper and cobalt. Orion Critical Mineral Consortium is negotiating with the international group Glencore for a 40-percent stake in its Mutanda and Kamoto mines, which also produce copper and cobalt. – Transparency probes? – Kinshasa urged Washington this month to “move from signed agreements to actual investments”. But the Democrats’ triumph in the US midterm elections could complicate the implementation of the partnerships concluded by the Trump administration amid questions about their transparency. The Democrats have already announced plans to open investigations early next year into the conditions under which the Trump administration conducted the negotiations. “Nothing should change in 2027 regarding the partnership principle, because the supply of minerals is of strategic national interest to the United States,” a mining source in the DRC told AFP. “The industry received bipartisan assurances on this issue in the run-up to the elections,” the source added. “But the agreements could be subject to opportunistic scrutiny by the Democrats, which might slow their implementation,” the source said. – Local economic benefits? – Several African countries have clearly demonstrated their determination to draw economic benefits from the partnerships. Zimbabwe suspended exports of raw minerals in February, ahead of a total ban in 2027, saying it would require processing and transformation to take place in the country. item.content:encoded: In 2026, the United States went on an economic offensive looking to access critical minerals across Africa in its race to compete with China for materials that are essential for new technologies and the energy transformation. Will 2027 deliver on these promises for African governments and will the new Democrat-controlled US Congress complicate US deals with investigations into their transparency? – Investments or promises? – American companies and consortiums this year announced large-scale mining investment projects through partnerships in Guinea, South Africa, Mozambique and Kenya. But it was the strategic partnership agreed in December 2025 with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) that illustrated Washington’s economic push to secure its supply of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China. China has had a long head-start. It began investing in the African mining sector in the 1990s. The deal stipulated that Kinshasa would identify a portfolio of mining assets on which American investors have a right of first offer. In return, the Congolese government secured diplomatic support from Washington on security in its volatile eastern region, rocked by violence by myriad armed groups for more than 30 years. Since then, the American company Virtus Minerals, in partnership with the Indian group Lloyds Metals&Energy, has announced the acquisition of Chemaf, a heavily indebted Congolese company specialising in copper and cobalt. Orion Critical Mineral Consortium is negotiating with the international group Glencore for a 40-percent stake in its Mutanda and Kamoto mines, which also produce copper and cobalt. – Transparency probes? – Kinshasa urged Washington this month to “move from signed agreements to actual investments”. But the Democrats’ triumph in the US midterm elections could complicate the implementation of the partnerships concluded by the Trump administration amid questions about their transparency. The Democrats have already announced plans to open investigations early next year into the conditions under which the Trump administration conducted the negotiations. “Nothing should change in 2027 regarding the partnership principle, because the supply of minerals is of strategic national interest to the United States,” a mining source in the DRC told AFP. “The industry received bipartisan assurances on this issue in the run-up to the elections,” the source added. “But the agreements could be subject to opportunistic scrutiny by the Democrats, which might slow their implementation,” the source said. – Local economic benefits? – Several African countries have clearly demonstrated their determination to draw economic benefits from the partnerships. Zimbabwe suspended exports of raw minerals in February, ahead of a total ban in 2027, saying it would require processing and transformation to take place in the country. The ban prompted mining companies to rush to build lithium processing plants, the first step in the value chain. A first factory, built by a Chinese company, is now operational. Others are planned. The DRC, the world’s leading cobalt producer, has suspended exports of the metal needed for top-range batteries from next month. The measure, which aims to shore up prices by preventing an over-supply on the market, had already been applied in February 2025 before a quota policy was introduced. “Our country has for a long time contributed to the wealth of industries around the world without keeping a sufficient amount of the added value to ensure its own economic transition,” Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi told a business conference in Kinshasa this week. In remarks to companies and banks at the same forum, Mines Minister Louis Watum assured “those who will carry out processing on our soil will find a partner in the government”. – Banking on rail? – Interest in the continent’s mineral resources has led to the implementation and completion of several major infrastructure projects. The goal of schemes such as Guinea’s large-scale Simandou iron ore mining project or the Lobito Corridor between the DRC and Angola is to secure and speed up the transportation of minerals to port, often by rail. While some of the mining output from the southern DRC is still transported in a constant stream of trucks to South African ports, another part now goes by rail to the Angolan port of Lobito on the Atlantic coast. Zambia is also involved in the EU- and US-financed Lobito project. So far, it has been the missing link but progress is expected in 2027 on a railway line project connecting the copper-producing region in the north to the existing line in Angola. – High-risk? – In some African countries, US investors remain cautious and demand guarantees to secure their investments. Talks are under way between the United States and the DRC in particular to improve the business climate in a country perceived as risky due to endemic corruption, an unpredictable tax system and weak legal protection. “Kinshasa expects concrete investments in 2027. But major changes should not be expected too quickly because mining projects take time,” Jacques Mukena, of the Ebuteli institute, said. The eastern conflict pitting armed anti-governmental forces backed by Rwanda against the Congolese army also continues, despite several mediation efforts. “Without progress on security, investors will remain cautious,” Mukena said. The post US targets Africa’s critical minerals to counter rivals appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Burnley 0-2 Birmingham City - fans' verdict
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley on Wednesday to make it an EFL record 24 home games without a win for the Clarets while Blues closed the gap at the top of the Championship. Here are some of your comments: Clarets fans Lynne: Tragic. No desire to push forward or take responsibility in front of goal. The fans are despondent as are the players. It's so sad to watch. Brian : The worst performance ever. Many will not renew season tickets until Pace has gone. Steve : Going backwards. Losing possession has been a problem all season, as has schoolboy defending. We are so so slow building attacks it's ridiculous. It's like we allow any team to get back in shape before we attack. Kyle Walker has been terrible and even Amdouni, who has been loved by the fans, has had stinkers in the last two games. I can see us going down again and the owners have created all this. They should resign as a board and sell up and go back to the US. Darren : Woeful, no fight in any of them. We are staring at League One football without a doubt. Mark : We were shocking. Our defence is about as useful as a chocolate fireguard. Vardy should have started, he'd have gotten on the end of Ramazani's crosses and balls into the box. It was a very lacklustre performance. On these performances we're down. Blues fans Phil : A routine win against a very poor team. In Blues' favour it's not the easiest place to visit on a cold winter evening. Gary : Good start but some sloppy play meant we needed Beadle to be on top form. Fry and Neumann excellent, Klarer has a rival for his place now, some puzzling substitutions from Davies. David : It's wins like this that win Championships and promotions. They build confidence which is so important. Daniel : Very professional performance, could have been more comfortable. Burnley had very good possession but no end product. Looking forward to upcoming games, real battle at the top now, bring it on. John : This win looks good but we could easily have lost if Burnley had taken their chances. In my opinion we were quite lucky in some ways.

item.title: Seven beautiful places to visit in GTA VI, from mountains trails to an afternoon at the zoo
item.description: Need a break from all the crime and violence? There are plenty of places to get away from it all in Leonida As Leonida goes, Mount Kalaga is the top of the world. There are bike trails and hiking trails all the way up the mountain, as well as plenty of hunting opportunities if that’s your thing. Shooting deer makes me sad, so instead I went birdwatching and spotted an eagle. Continue reading...

item.title: Much-needed rotations, Balde’s statement | Three takeaways from Sabah 1-4 Barcelona
item.description: Much-needed rotations, Balde’s statement | Three takeaways from Sabah 1-4 Barcelona Barcelona put four goals past Sabah FC at Baku last night in an early kickoff in the UEFA Champions League, cementing their place in the top-8 and taking another step forward. Anthony Gordon opened the scoring in the first half and handed the team a small cushion at half-time, one that he himself extended with a second goal soon after the break. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus then joined the party and made it 4-0 for Barcelona, putting the result in stone and ensuring the three points. Sabah’s consolation goal arrived in the 63rd minute and remains as a small black mark on the result for Barcelona. Nevertheless, the Catalans will remain optimistic and positive after the win, given how all other factors played out in their favour. Barca Universal brings you three takeaways from Sabah 1-4 Barcelona. Much-needed rotations There has been much discourse about Barcelona’s hectic schedule over the next few weeks, especially with big tests including Manchester City yet to arrive. Hansi Flick made several changes to his starting XI against Sabah. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) In that sense, the game last night provided Hansi Flick with a crucial chance to make rotations, and the manager made the most of his chance. Given the relatively weak opponents on the night, Flick kept several key starters out of the dynamics and handed a chance to fringe players. For starters, Alejandro Balde entered the starting XI in place of Joao Cancelo while Pau Cubarsi continued to be on the bench for the second-straight game and garnered much-needed rest. Eric Garcia was another regular name who stayed on the bench on the night as Flick handed Jules Kounde an opportunity to prove his worth. In midfield, Flick handed Gavi a rare start alongside Pedri and Fermin Lopez, thereby resting Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal. Lamine Yamal stayed completely out of the squad while Raphinha was also left out of the starting lineup. Instead, it was the trio of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus who started and delivered the lethal blows on the night. Handing so many starters a much-needed rest, needless to say, will go a long way in helping Barcelona tackle the stress of the calendar. Alejandro Balde’s statement Balde has not had it easy this season, and the manager’s clear preference towards other players at left-back has been very apparent. Alejandro Balde played a fantastic game vs Sabah. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His start against Sabah, thus, arrived as a massive surprise that not many saw coming, and he did not disappoint. In 64 minutes on the field last night, Balde ensured to make himself an attacking menace as he continually attacked the Sabah box with purpose and created chances for fun. He racked up one assist, created one big chance and had one key pass on the night while also completing 94% of his passes. Further, he had two successful dribbles, eight progressive carries
item.content:encoded: Much-needed rotations, Balde’s statement | Three takeaways from Sabah 1-4 Barcelona Barcelona put four goals past Sabah FC at Baku last night in an early kickoff in the UEFA Champions League, cementing their place in the top-8 and taking another step forward. Anthony Gordon opened the scoring in the first half and handed the team a small cushion at half-time, one that he himself extended with a second goal soon after the break. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus then joined the party and made it 4-0 for Barcelona, putting the result in stone and ensuring the three points. Sabah’s consolation goal arrived in the 63rd minute and remains as a small black mark on the result for Barcelona. Nevertheless, the Catalans will remain optimistic and positive after the win, given how all other factors played out in their favour. Barca Universal brings you three takeaways from Sabah 1-4 Barcelona. Much-needed rotations There has been much discourse about Barcelona’s hectic schedule over the next few weeks, especially with big tests including Manchester City yet to arrive. Hansi Flick made several changes to his starting XI against Sabah. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) In that sense, the game last night provided Hansi Flick with a crucial chance to make rotations, and the manager made the most of his chance. Given the relatively weak opponents on the night, Flick kept several key starters out of the dynamics and handed a chance to fringe players. For starters, Alejandro Balde entered the starting XI in place of Joao Cancelo while Pau Cubarsi continued to be on the bench for the second-straight game and garnered much-needed rest. Eric Garcia was another regular name who stayed on the bench on the night as Flick handed Jules Kounde an opportunity to prove his worth. In midfield, Flick handed Gavi a rare start alongside Pedri and Fermin Lopez, thereby resting Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal. Lamine Yamal stayed completely out of the squad while Raphinha was also left out of the starting lineup. Instead, it was the trio of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus who started and delivered the lethal blows on the night. Handing so many starters a much-needed rest, needless to say, will go a long way in helping Barcelona tackle the stress of the calendar. Alejandro Balde’s statement Balde has not had it easy this season, and the manager’s clear preference towards other players at left-back has been very apparent. Alejandro Balde played a fantastic game vs Sabah. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His start against Sabah, thus, arrived as a massive surprise that not many saw coming, and he did not disappoint. In 64 minutes on the field last night, Balde ensured to make himself an attacking menace as he continually attacked the Sabah box with purpose and created chances for fun. He racked up one assist, created one big chance and had one key pass on the night while also completing 94% of his passes. Further, he had two successful dribbles, eight progressive carries and a staggering 23 carries on the night. For a player who is being pushed out of the spotlight, his performance arrived as a massive statement of his quality. It remains uncertain if his future will be in Catalonia, and he gave his best shot at making one final plea to the manager to reconsider his stance. Even if a departure is on the cards, his performance last night will go a long way in attracting better interest. A step closer Barcelona’s win over Sabah last night was anything but perfect, and while the opponents did not create too many chances of their own, one would have expected the Catalans to come out more dominant. Barcelona are currently fourth in the UCL table. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) They did not create as many effective chances as they usually do, nor were the forwards nearly as effective. It was clear that the forwards lacked coordination – something understandable given the rotations. Considering the full picture of the rotations and how the team still managed to score four goals, however, Hansi Flick and Co. will gladly accept the results. After all, Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus all managed to enter the scoresheet. Moreover, they created nine big chances, and it was only the finishing which was off the mark. With the result last night comes a sense of comfort in the UEFA Champions League, for Barcelona are now fourth in the standings with twelve points in five games. They only sit behind Real Madrid, PSG and Como, and the win last night helps them take a step forward. One more win in the competition will be enough to all but seal their place in the top-eight. They face Manchester City next, and should they find a way to beat the Blues, even a top-2 finish cannot be ruled out. In that sense, the win last night comes as a massive step forward that the team desperately needed.

item.title: Experienced Real Madrid defender misses another chance to impress Jose Mourinho
item.description: Experienced Real Madrid defender misses another chance to impress Jose Mourinho During the early phase of the campaign, Real Madrid fans were yearning for the return of Eder Militao from injury. The Brazilian international is widely considered the de facto leader of the Real Madrid defence, due to his experience and the consistency he has shown in the past. After yet another long injury spell, Militao eventually received the medical clearance earlier in the season, but his road to the first team has been much more difficult than expected. Jose Mourinho has been very careful in integrating Militao into the starting eleven, giving him opportunities primarily in Champions League matches. Militao fails yet again Time for Militao to step up his game. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) However, in those limited opportunities, Militao hasn’t really been able to show that he should be Real Madrid’s starting centre-back. Indeed, the Brazilian has featured in both UCL games against AEK Athens and PSV Eindhoven, and he has struggled in both. A start against Militao was an excellent opportunity for Militao to prove himself. But he had a disastrous start to the proceedings and was completely overrun by the speedy PSV frontline. Mourinho eventually made the decision to bench him at half-time. In the two matches Militao has started this season, Real Madrid have conceded three goals and are yet to keep a clean sheet. Konate and Huijsen remain the top choice options Militao’s form has been concerning for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Militao’s relatively poor performances suggest he is not yet ready to become a first-team regular in the Real Madrid setup. Whether or not that is because of his fitness remains to be seen. But for now, it appears Mourinho has clearly identified Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen as his first-choice options in central defence. Antonio Rudiger is another option for Mourinho. But much like Militao, the German veteran also struggled to keep up with the PSV attack this midweek and was replaced at half-time. This is a sign of a broader issue at Real Madrid, where Mourinho has observed that second-fiddle players have failed to offer the same quality as his first-choice stars. The coming weeks, therefore, could prove to be crucial for Militao as he looks to regain full fitness and provide some strong performances, which in turn may help him push for a regular starting role at the heart of Los Blancos backline.

item.title: Kabayel vs Hysa: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight this weekend
item.description: This weekend, Agit Kabayel will make his first defence of the WBC heavyweight title, taking on Nelson Hysa in a battle of unbeaten boxers. Kabayel, 34, will fight on home soil in Germany as he takes on his Albanian foe, 42, in what is a brave new era at heavyweight. Over the last year or so, Oleksandr Usyk has vacated all four of the major titles , with Kabayel elevated from interim WBC champion as a result. The unbeaten Agit Kabayel is the WBC heavyweight champion (Getty) But before the German can go in search of unification fights against Daniel Dubois, Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev, he must see off Hysa, who has scored 23 KOs across 25 wins. Here’s all you need to know: When is the fight? Kabayel vs Hysa will take place on Saturday 28 November at Esprit Arena in Dusseldorf, Germany. The main card will begin at 6pm GMT (10am PT / 12pm CT / 1pm ET), with main-event ring walks expected at around 10pm GMT (2pm PT / 4pm CT / 5pm ET). How can I watch it? The event will stream live exclusively on DAZN. You can purchase a DAZN subscription here , with plans starting at £25.99 per month. Odds Kabayel – 1/12 Hysa – 6/1 Draw – 20/1 Via William Hill . Nelson Hysa (top) last fought in August, stopping Thomas Narmo in two rounds (Getty) Get all the latest boxing betting sites’ offers. item.title: The Lord of the Rings’ Next Movie Officially Wraps Production, but Now the Hard Part Begins
item.description: Warner Bros. announced on Nov. 25, 2026, that production on the next installment in The Lord of the Rings movie franchise has wrapped. The Hunt for Gollum , directed by Andy Serkis, is currently headed for post-production ahead of the movie's Dec. 17, 2027 release. The news follows Serkis' announcement in November that filming had ended .

item.title: Celtic linked with a move for Belarus goalkeeper Fedor Lapoukhov
item.description: Celtic linked with a move for Belarus goalkeeper Fedor Lapoukhov Celtic has been linked with a move for Belarus shot-stopper Fedor Lapoukhov but not in the January transfer window… Fedor Lapoukhov of Dinamo Minsk during during the UEFA Conference League match between Panathinaikos FC and FC Dinamo-Minsk at on December 19, 2024 in Athens, Greece. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) Celtic are reportedly keeping tabs on Belarus International goalkeeper Fedor Lapoukhov as Martin O’Neill looks to bolster his options between the sticks. The Belarus international faced Scotland at Hampden last year and has been monitored by Celtic ever since according to reports. It is understood that Celtic’s interest is a more long term one, with a view to a bid next summer as opposed to the upcoming January transfer window. The 23 years old 6ft 3 shot-stopper plays his club football for Bulgarian side CSKA Sofia, and has already amassed 20 caps for the Belarusian national side, and played against Scotland in the World Cup qualifiers last year. Fedor Lapoukhov of Belarus fails to save as Gustav Isaksen of Denmark scores his team’s second goal during the FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifier match between Denmark and Belarus at Parken Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Copenhagen, Denmark. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) Lapoukhov started his career in his native Belarus with FC Dynamo Minsk and was part of two league title winning sides, before joining CSKA Sofia last summer, helping his new side win the Bulgarian national cup as well as the Super Cup in his first full season. The 23 year old who is contracted to the Bulgarians until the summer of 2028 is valued at around £2.5 million. A look at Fedor Lapoukhov’s Playing Profile and Strengths Goalkeeper, Fedor Lapoukhov of Belarus in action during the FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifier match between Denmark and Belarus at Parken Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Copenhagen, Denmark. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) Shot-Stopping & 1v1s: Uses his frame well to narrow angles in one-versus-one situations and shows sharp reflexes from close range. In the 2026–27 First Professional League, Footystats records an 80.43% save rate (37 saves from 46 shots faced) and 4 clean sheets across 11 league appearances (0.73 goals conceded per 90). Aerial & Cross Handling: As you’d imagine he’s Confident at claiming and dealing with crosses inside the penalty area, backed by a 1.90 m frame. Distribution & Composure: Calm starting moves from deeper areas; scouting databases such as FM Scout and FMinside highlight strong left-footedness, while FotMob notes his regular minutes in the 2026–27 league campaign. Areas to Develop Consistency & Decision-Making: Occasional lapses in judgment and game-to-game fluctuations remain key areas to refine as he steps up against higher-tempo opposition. Lapoukhov is clearly a player of great potential. Is a move to Celtic on the cards? Wonder what the chaps at Pluto Data Analytics make of him and

item.title: ESPN’s Desmond Howard Makes His Stance Clear on Alabama’s Controversial Ranking
item.description: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; ESPN personality Desmond Howard arrives at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During Wednesday’s edition of ESPN’s “Get Up,” Howard discussed the committee’s decision to move Alabama from No. 3 to No. 6. The Crimson Tide fell behind Texas, Notre Dame and Tennessee despite improving to 9-2 with Saturday’s victory over Chattanooga. However, Howard believes the committee made the correct decision. “I thought they finally got it right,” Howard said. The ESPN analyst questioned why Alabama had remained ahead of teams with stronger victories in previous rankings. In particular, Howard pointed toward Texas and its collection of quality wins. The Longhorns moved to No. 3 after spending recent weeks behind Alabama. Howard Points to a Major Difference Between Alabama and Texas Howard believes the committee should prioritize the quality of each team’s victories when evaluating playoff contenders. Texas has defeated Ohio State, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU this season. Meanwhile, Alabama does not currently own a victory over a team ranked in the committee’s latest top 25. That difference played a significant role in Howard’s assessment. The analyst also questioned why Texas had remained behind Alabama despite its stronger collection of ranked victories. item.content:encoded: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; ESPN personality Desmond Howard arrives at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During Wednesday’s edition of ESPN’s “Get Up,” Howard discussed the committee’s decision to move Alabama from No. 3 to No. 6. The Crimson Tide fell behind Texas, Notre Dame and Tennessee despite improving to 9-2 with Saturday’s victory over Chattanooga. However, Howard believes the committee made the correct decision. “I thought they finally got it right,” Howard said. The ESPN analyst questioned why Alabama had remained ahead of teams with stronger victories in previous rankings. In particular, Howard pointed toward Texas and its collection of quality wins. The Longhorns moved to No. 3 after spending recent weeks behind Alabama. Howard Points to a Major Difference Between Alabama and Texas Howard believes the committee should prioritize the quality of each team’s victories when evaluating playoff contenders. Texas has defeated Ohio State, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU this season. Meanwhile, Alabama does not currently own a victory over a team ranked in the committee’s latest top 25. That difference played a significant role in Howard’s assessment. The analyst also questioned why Texas had remained behind Alabama despite its stronger collection of ranked victories. For Howard, the results on the field should carry more weight than a team’s reputation. His comments add another prominent ESPN voice to the debate surrounding Alabama’s playoff résumé. Tennessee Also Moves Ahead of Alabama Texas wasn’t the only SEC program to pass Alabama in Tuesday’s rankings. Tennessee climbed to No. 5, moving one position ahead of the Crimson Tide. The Volunteers defeated Alabama 26-10 earlier this season, giving Tennessee a valuable head-to-head advantage. However, Alabama had remained ahead of Tennessee in previous committee rankings. That changed Tuesday after the Volunteers improved their record with a victory over LSU. College Football Playoff selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek explained that the committee had reevaluated the teams’ résumés. The latest rankings now place Texas third, Tennessee fifth and Alabama sixth. All three programs enter rivalry weekend with identical 9-2 records. Alabama Faces Important Iron Bowl Test Howard’s comments arrive just days before Alabama hosts Auburn in the annual Iron Bowl. The Crimson Tide will welcome the Tigers to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28. Alabama enters the matchup with an opportunity to strengthen its playoff position and preserve its conference championship hopes. Meanwhile, Auburn will attempt to disrupt those ambitions. item.title: Midweek Warm-up: What a week for Bayern Munich, huh?; Don’t meet your heroes; Champions League predictions; and MORE!
item.description: Photo: Peter Kneffel/dpa (Photo by Peter Kneffel/picture alliance via Getty Images) “What a week, huh?” “Captain, it’s Wednesday.” Bayern Munich could probably use that exchange as the unofficial motto for the last several d ays. Between the public discussion surrounding J amal Musiala, comments from club leadership, questions about his contract, and now reporting from Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (via @iMiaSan Mia ) about Vincent Kompany reassuring players and club employees regarding Musia la’s health, it has been an exhausting news cycle. According to Falk and Agardi, Kompany told his players during a dressing-room team talk that they should have absolutely no concerns about Musiala or his health, assuring them that their teammate is in excellent health and full of energy. Kompany reportedly delivered the same reassurance to several other club employees. The reassurance comes after a week in which Musiala has seemingly become the center of a wider Bayern Munich debate that has extended well beyond football. Comments and crit icism from Jan-Christian Dreesen, Uli Hoeneß, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge regarding Musiala, his contract, and his situation have helped fuel the perception of a growing divide between the player a nd the club. What might ordinarily be an internal conversation about a player’s development, recovery, contractual future, and expectations has increasingly played out publicly, leaving Musiala at the center of a debate that is difficult to separate from the footballing realities. That is where this entire situation has become particularly uncomfortable. Musiala is not just a contract negotiat ion, a talking point for club executives, or a headline generator. He is a player recovering, trying to get back to his best, and one whose importance to Bayern Munich is difficult to oversta te. Public discourse can easily turn a complicated situation into a perceived confrontation, but that does not necessarily reflect what is happening behind closed doors. Ultimately, though, thi s is about Jamal Musiala’s health. The hope should be that he gets fully healthy, regains his confidence, and returns to the form that made him one of the mo st highly regarded talents in world football. That is what matters most, regardless of the noise, the speculation, or the conversations about who knew what and when. Will he get back to a top level? Is he worth the massive contract? Should Bayern Munich seek to renegotiate? For now, it is probably time to put th is ordeal aside, take a breath, and focus on what Bayern Munich actually has in front of it — a Champions League game. The rest can wait. Song of the Midweek: “Young Again” by Shinedown In contrast to our normal fare, here is a newer song. Released earlier this year on EI8HT , this one caught my attention, and it felt like a good little change from a lot of my reminiscing about music from years closer to my prime (hell yeah!). Enjoy: In lieu of an Entertainment Rundown As the podcast

According to Falk and Agardi, Kompany told his players during a dressing-room team talk that they should have absolutely no concerns about Musiala or his health, assuring them that their teammate is in excellent health and full of energy. Kompany reportedly delivered the same reassurance to several other club employees. The reassurance comes after a week in which Musiala has seemingly become the center of a wider Bayern Munich debate that has extended well beyond football. Comments and crit icism from Jan-Christian Dreesen, Uli Hoeneß, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge regarding Musiala, his contract, and his situation have helped fuel the perception of a growing divide between the player a nd the club. What might ordinarily be an internal conversation about a player’s development, recovery, contractual future, and expectations has increasingly played out publicly, leaving Musiala at the center of a debate that is difficult to separate from the footballing realities. That is where this entire situation has become particularly uncomfortable. Musiala is not just a contract negotiat ion, a talking point for club executives, or a headline generator. He is a player recovering, trying to get back to his best, and one whose importance to Bayern Munich is difficult to oversta te. Public discourse can easily turn a complicated situation into a perceived confrontation, but that does not necessarily reflect what is happening behind closed doors. Ultimately, though, thi s is about Jamal Musiala’s health. The hope should be that he gets fully healthy, regains his confidence, and returns to the form that made him one of the mo st highly regarded talents in world football. That is what matters most, regardless of the noise, the speculation, or the conversations about who knew what and when. Will he get back to a top level? Is he worth the massive contract? Should Bayern Munich seek to renegotiate? For now, it is probably time to put th is ordeal aside, take a breath, and focus on what Bayern Munich actually has in front of it — a Champions League game. The rest can wait. Song of the Midweek: “Young Again” by Shinedown In contrast to our normal fare, here is a newer song. Released earlier this year on EI8HT , this one caught my attention, and it felt like a good little change from a lot of my reminiscing about music from years closer to my prime (hell yeah!). Enjoy: In lieu of an Entertainment Rundown As the podcast listeners know, I’ve been on the road a bit and had no time to watch anything, but there is a topic that needs to be addressed… Manuel Neuer has found himself caught up in yet ano ther controversy, and while the latest discussion surrounding the Bayern Munich captain might change how some people view him personally, it should not change how we evalua te him as a footballer. Those two things can coexist, even if football fandom often struggles to separate them. There is an uncomfortable reality in sports — exceptional athletes are not necessarily exceptional people. Players can make questionable dec isions, display narcissistic tendencies, behave selfishly, or even be genuinely unpleasant individuals, and still be extraordinary at their profession. Football does not automatically mak e someone virtuous, and talent does not require a spotless personal record. Neuer’s legacy as one of the greatest goalkeepers of his generation is built on what he has done between the posts, not on whether every decision he has made away from the pitch deserves admiration. Criticism of his conduct is fair, and fans are perfectly enti tled to reassess the person they thought they knew. But that does not erase decades of elite performances. It is another reminder of the old saying, “Do not meet your heroes.” Sometimes the person behind the legend is considerably more complicated than the image we built in our heads. That does not mean the football was any less phenomenal. Predictions When I look in the mirror I can’t believe what I see Tell me, who’s that funky dude Staring back at me? Broken, beaten down, can’t even get around Without an old man cane, I fall and hit the ground Shivering in the cold, I’m bitter and alone Excuse the b*tching I shouldn’t complain I should have no feeling ‘Cause feeling is pain As everything I need is denied me And everything I want is taken away from me But who do I got to blame? Nobody but me Yup, Bayern Munich is, indeed, broken and beaten down and not living “The Good Life” — at least not at this very moment. At some point, though, the squad has to get past t he headlines and conjecture and remember why it is here in the first place: a Champions League tilt vs. LOSC Lille. LOSC Lille is not great, let alone a powerhouse, but it has — at least — had a week not mired in controversy. In addition, while Lille does have some injuries, its front line is mostly intact. The same cannot be said for Bayern Munich, which is limping into the game. At some point, though, the pride wi thin the Bavarians has to show through all of the nonsense going on around the squad. The fight and heart will need to be on full display, and the mentality of a true champion will either be there when the whistle blows or… it won’t. Let’s bank on Bayern Munich remembering exactly who the (expletive removed) it is. And I don’t wanna be an old man anymore It’s been a year or two since I was out on the floor Shakin’ booty, makin’ sweet love all the night It’s time I got back to the good life Prediction: Lille 1-2 Bayern Munich (L) Other Champions League predictions include: Tuesday November 24th Bodø/Glimt 2-1 LASK Linz (W) Galatasaray 1-2 Aston Villa (L) Arsenal 1-0 Borussia Dortmund (L) Como 3-1 AEK Athens (W) Feyenoord 2-2 FC Porto (L) Manchester City 4-1 Napoli (L) RB Leipzig 3-0 Lens (W) Real Madrid 4-1 PSV Eindhoven (W) Slovan Bratislava 0-2 Real Betis (W) Tuesday’s record: 5-4, 1PP Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Sabah FK 0-5 FC Barcelona (W) Slavia Prague 1-2 Villarreal (W) Atlético Madrid 2-0 Viking FK (W) Club Brugge 1-3 Liverpool (W) Inter Milan 2-1 VfB Stuttgart (W) Paris Saint-Germain 2-1 AS Roma (this game will tell us a lot about PSG’s fight-or-flight mentality) (L) Shakhtar Donetsk 0-1 Fenerbahçe (W)*** Sporting CP 1-2 Manchester United (L) Wednesday’s record: 6-3, 1PP Prediction Records Total: 356-214 Perfect Picks: 50 Bundesliga Last Matchday: 5-4 Bundesliga Overall: 44-46 DFB-Pokal: 40-8 World Cup: 71-28 International Friendlies: 50-30 UEFA Nations League: 90-66 Champions League: 55-35 Club Friendlies: 5-1 Franz Beckenbauer Supercup: 1-0 Join the conversation!
