item.title: VCU wins on another clutch game-winner for 2nd game in a row
item.description: MT1USATODAY28561151 VCU wins on another clutch game-winner for 2nd game in a row appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . VCU pulled off another last-minute escape at the Maui Invitational, overcoming Washington 80-78 behind guard Nyk Lewis’ game-winning heroics Wednesday night in Lahaina. Lewis connected on a jumper in the paint with just seconds remaining to complete VCU’s comeback and improve its record to 5-2. The win came a day after guard Blake Harper hit a 45-foot buzzer-beater to give the Rams an 84-81 win over Colorado State. VCU wins it late for a second straight night 🔥 @VCU_Hoops https://t.co/JWvXOxYf6E pic.twitter.com/QsfyH3WrbJ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) November 26, 2026 VCU trailed by as many as 10 points in the second half against the Huskies but finished the contest with an 8-1 run. Washington appeared to be in control late, holding a 77-72 advantage after forward Nikola Dzepina converted two free throws with 2:47 remaining. However, Harper knocked down four free throws before Lewis added two more, putting the Rams ahead 78-77 with approximately 24 seconds left. Huskies guard Ryan Beasley then made one of his two free-throw attempts to level the score at 78-78 with 12 seconds remaining. Following a timeout, Lewis drove into the lane and converted the decisive jumper. Washington had one final opportunity, but Dzepina’s long-range attempt bounced off the back of the rim as time expired. Forward Torey Alston led VCU with 19 points off the bench, while Harper contributed 17. Junior guards Ahmad Nowell and Brandon Jennings also contributed 13 points apiece. Meanwhile, Dzepina finished with a career-best performance for the Huskies, recording 31 points while shooting 7-of-9 from beyond the arc. LeJuan Watts added 17 points and nine rebounds for Washington, which fell to 5-2. The Huskies held a 42-41 halftime advantage after a first half featuring nine lead changes and six ties. Washington also maintained its advantage throughout the second half until the Rams’ late comeback. Both teams finished shooting 50% from the field. The Huskies connected on 13 of its 23 three-point attempts, compared to VCU’s 8-of-22 performance. Washington also controlled the boards 33-23 but committed 17 turnovers that resulted in 19 points for the Rams. The Huskies went without a made field goal over the final 3:43, allowing VCU to complete another late comeback. Up next, the Rams will return home to face Coppin State on December 3. item.description: Argentina's head coach Lionel Scaloni gives instructions to Argentina's forward #10 Lionel Messi during the 2026 World Cup round of 32 football match between Argentina and Cape Verde at the Miami Stadium in Miami Gardens on July 3, 2026. (Photo by PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA / AFP via Getty Images) Getty NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 17: Lionel Scaloni, Head Coach of Argentina, and Lionel Messi #10 of Argentina interact on stage ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final between Spain and Argentina at Fanatics Fest at Javits Center on July 17, 2026 in New York, New York. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) Getty BUENOS AIRES, ARGENTINA - OCTOBER 06: Lionel Messi of Argentina celebrates scoring his team's third goal during the International Friendly match between Argentina and Benin at Estadio Monumental Antonio V. Liberti on October 06, 2026 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Lionel Messi is making his final appearance for Argentina following his announcement of international retirement on 31 August. (Photo by Marcelo Endelli/Getty Images) Getty Lionel Messi may have played his final game for Argentina, but his time with the national team might not be over just yet. Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has opened the door for the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner to join his coaching staff following the departure of longtime assistant Walter Samuel. Speaking to reporters ahead of Argentina’s November friendly against Costa Rica, Scaloni addressed the possibility of reuniting with his former captain in a different capacity. “Now that Walter [Samuel] is no longer here, let him come,” Scaloni said, according to beIN Sports. Scaloni, however, does not expect Messi to hang up his cleats anytime soon. The Argentina coach believes the 39-year-old Inter Miami superstar could continue playing beyond 2030. Nevertheless, the prospect of Messi returning to the national team in a coaching capacity adds an intriguing dimension to Argentina’s next World Cup cycle. Lionel Messi Could Reunite With Lionel Scaloni Getty Lionel Scaloni, Head Coach of Argentina, and Lionel Messi of Argentina interact on stage ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final between Spain and Argentina at Fanatics Fest at Javits Center on July 17, 2026 in New York, New York. The possibility of a reunion comes at a significant turning point for Argentine soccer. Scaloni agreed to a contract extension through July 2030 on November 12, according to Reuters . (Photo by PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA / AFP via Getty Images) Getty NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 17: Lionel Scaloni, Head Coach of Argentina, and Lionel Messi #10 of Argentina interact on stage ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final between Spain and Argentina at Fanatics Fest at Javits Center on July 17, 2026 in New York, New York. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) Getty BUENOS AIRES, ARGENTINA - OCTOBER 06: Lionel Messi of Argentina celebrates scoring his team's third goal during the International Friendly match between Argentina and Benin at Estadio Monumental Antonio V. Liberti on October 06, 2026 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Lionel Messi is making his final appearance for Argentina following his announcement of international retirement on 31 August. (Photo by Marcelo Endelli/Getty Images) Getty Lionel Messi may have played his final game for Argentina, but his time with the national team might not be over just yet. Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has opened the door for the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner to join his coaching staff following the departure of longtime assistant Walter Samuel. Speaking to reporters ahead of Argentina’s November friendly against Costa Rica, Scaloni addressed the possibility of reuniting with his former captain in a different capacity. “Now that Walter [Samuel] is no longer here, let him come,” Scaloni said, according to beIN Sports. Scaloni, however, does not expect Messi to hang up his cleats anytime soon. The Argentina coach believes the 39-year-old Inter Miami superstar could continue playing beyond 2030. Nevertheless, the prospect of Messi returning to the national team in a coaching capacity adds an intriguing dimension to Argentina’s next World Cup cycle. Lionel Messi Could Reunite With Lionel Scaloni Getty Lionel Scaloni, Head Coach of Argentina, and Lionel Messi of Argentina interact on stage ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final between Spain and Argentina at Fanatics Fest at Javits Center on July 17, 2026 in New York, New York. The possibility of a reunion comes at a significant turning point for Argentine soccer. Scaloni agreed to a contract extension through July 2030 on November 12, according to Reuters . The extension puts Scaloni in position to become the first coach in Argentina’s history to lead the national team at three consecutive World Cups. Meanwhile, Samuel’s departure ends an eight-year partnership with Scaloni that produced a World Cup championship and two Copa América titles. The former Argentina and Inter Milan defender intends to pursue a career as a head coach. Messi’s familiarity with Scaloni’s system and his relationships with Argentina’s established players could make him a valuable addition to the staff. However, there is no indication that Messi intends to pursue coaching once his playing career ends. For now, Scaloni must navigate Argentina’s transition without the player who helped define his tenure. Argentina Faces Challenges Beyond Lionel Messi’s Retirement Getty Lionel Messi of Argentina celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the International Friendly match between Argentina and Benin at Estadio Monumental Antonio V. Liberti on October 06, 2026 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Lionel Messi is making his final appearance for Argentina following his announcement of international retirement on 31 August. Argentina received an early reminder of that challenge when it lost 2-1 to Uruguay on November 13 in its first international match following Messi’s retirement. The national team still features several established stars, including Julián Álvarez, Lautaro Martínez, Enzo Fernández and Alexis Mac Allister. However, replacing Messi’s influence extends beyond finding another creative force on the field. Argentina’s international success during the Messi era transformed the national team into a global commercial powerhouse. The Argentine Football Association’s commercial portfolio has grown to 90 brands worldwide, with sponsorship agreements involving Adidas, Coca-Cola, Google Gemini, Lay’s and Airbnb. The federation also expanded into digital entertainment through regional sponsorship agreements, including its 2024 partnership with online poker platform Coin Poker . Adidas, meanwhile, extended its agreement with the federation through 2038, a commitment that stretches well beyond Messi’s playing career. Maintaining that global appeal without its most recognizable player presents another challenge for the federation. Messi retired from international soccer in October with a national-record 126 goals in 208 appearances. He helped Argentina reach consecutive World Cup finals, winning the trophy in Qatar in 2022 before falling to Spain in 2026. His international playing career may be over, but Scaloni has made it clear there is still room for him. Whether Messi eventually chooses to exchange his iconic No. 10 jersey for a place on Argentina’s bench remains entirely up to him. item.title: Rugby Paper Roundup: All Blacks in crisis? England’s rise & Beauden Barrett to Bristol Bears
item.description: Are the All Blacks in serious decline, or has the rest of the rugby world finally caught up? After New Zealand ‘s historic defeat to Wales and record loss against England, Two Cents Rugby joins The Rugby Paper Roundup to debate the biggest talking points in international rugby. We discuss what ‘ s going wrong under Dave Rennie, Will Jordan’s injury blow and Beauden Barrett’s reported move to Bristol Bears after the 2027 Rugby World Cup . Plus, are Steve Borthwick ‘s England genuine World Cup contenders? Are South Africa becoming vulnerable after consecutive defeats? item.title: 'We play with no fear!' - Mario Hermoso reveals Gian Piero Gasperini's training ground secret after AS Roma halt Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack. Hermoso inspires fearless Roma to historic Paris point Mario Hermoso set the tone inside five minutes as AS Roma held reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain to a thrilling 2-2 draw in the first-ever meeting between the clubs on Wednesday night. Winning possession high up the pitch before finishing from Matias Soule's cut-back, the Spanish centre-back helped Gian Piero Gasperini's side end PSG's 100 per cent Champions League start despite goals from Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele, with substitute Donyell Malen converting a late penalty after Vitinha's handball. "Everyone knows what the coach does, this is his identity, his style of playing," Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia after collecting UEFA's Player of the Match award. "We defenders get the opportunity to be protagonists, so I am very happy to come to a stadium like this, and see Roma playing in this special way, with no fear. We are on the right track and must keep taking these big steps forward." Training ground drills and Gasperini's squad rotation Gasperini sprang a tactical surprise by leaving Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante on the bench from the start, yet Roma's rotated line-up matched the French giants across 90 minutes. Hermoso, who also went close to adding a second open-play goal, revealed how attacking rotations are rehearsed daily. "With these team-mates who play in attack, we do try to make these moves in training sessions, everyone gets to have a go, and that means us defenders can bring something extra to the team, it's an added benefit," he explained. Addressing the bench impact, Hermoso added: "Everyone in this squad is important, we are set out in a way that we can all be protagonists. Dony, Paulo and Bryan had more minutes in this season, but they came on with the right mentality, and were ready to help get a good result." Building a winning mentality against European champions PSG only breached Roma's open-play organisation through Zabarnyi's 31st-minute corner header and Dembele's 62nd-minute spot-kick after Achraf Hakimi was fouled by Wesley. Hermoso credited Gasperini with transforming Roma's resilience in high-pressure European fixtures. "The coach gives you confidence to believe, to have this mentality of reacting to difficult moments that we suffered not just this season, but over the years," Hermoso told Prime Video . "This is important, given the way the team came in, the way we played this match against a team that has won the last two Champions Leagues. The result is a huge achievement... It's a shame we didn't win, but a point is good." Roma target knockout surge from 25th place Sitting second in Serie A, Roma now

item.title: Europa League: Olympiacos vs. Milan – Probable line-ups and where to watch on TV
item.description: Europa League: Olympiacos vs. Milan – Probable line-ups and where to watch on TV Ruben Amorim and Milan find themselves in need of points in the Europa League table and are preparing for a tough test away against the unbeaten Olympiacos in Athens on Thursday evening. The Rossoneri have won just one and lost three of their first four matches in the Europa League this season, and will be tasked with taking on Olympiacos, who have three wins and one draw on their record so far this term. ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Lenny Joseph of Ferencvarosi TC scores his team’s second goal under pressure from Mario Gila of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Milan were victorious on their return to action over the weekend following the recent international break, putting five past Frosinone in a dominant display that brought goals from Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic. They will be without nine players for Thursday’s clash with Olympiacos, though. Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers, Samuel Chukwueze, Francesco Camarda, David Bartesaghi and Pierro Terracciano are all expected to be unavailable this evening. That means that Amorim is unable to make too many alterations to the side that beat Frosinone over the weekend. Permission Estupinan is set to replace Bartesaghi at left-back, Ardon Jashari could come into the starting XI and Omari Hutchinson could also be introduced to the attack. Kick-off this evening is due at 17.45 GMT. Olympiacos vs. Milan: Probable line-ups ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Players of AC Milan pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Olympiacos (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Pirola, Bruno; Freuler Gustavo Sà; Gelson Martins, Fortounis, Jota Silva, Gonzalez. Milan (4-4-1-1): Maignan, Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Hutchinson, Jashari, Rabiot, Moreira; Pulisic; Ramos. Where to watch Olympiacos vs. Milan ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, looks on before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Tonight’s game will be available to watch live in the UK on TNT Sports 4 and online through HBO Max. Supporters in the USA are able to tune in via Paramount+. Join us for all the pre-match build-up, in-game coverage and post-match reactions on the Football Italia Liveblog.

item.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. According to him, the weapons were returned to the plane, which Nigerian soldiers then surrounded to ensure they were not smuggled out later. Fani-Kayode said the reason for the President’s firmness became clear at the next cabinet meeting. “As for my boss OBJ, he saved lives on that day by putting his foot down and insisting that the heavy weapons must not be let in because, as I was later told when the matter was discussed at the next cab

item.content:encoded: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. According to him, the weapons were returned to the plane, which Nigerian soldiers then surrounded to ensure they were not smuggled out later. Fani-Kayode said the reason for the President’s firmness became clear at the next cabinet meeting. “As for my boss OBJ, he saved lives on that day by putting his foot down and insisting that the heavy weapons must not be let in because, as I was later told when the matter was discussed at the next cabinet meeting, what the Libyans had done in the past when they carried in such weapons was to hand them over to their local associates and leave them behind. “Those lethal weapons would later become part of a stockpile of arms that provided a massive arsenal for terrorists, insurgents and other ruthless non-state actors within our country,” he said. He said the standoff taught him that “firmness, the display of mutual respect and a strict adherence to the rules of engagement were vital”, adding that the Libyan delegation showed Nigeria “massive respect” from that moment. Fani-Kayode recalled that Gaddafi was killed in his home town, Sirte, on October 20, 2011, and that he watched the footage with sadness. “This was a clear and graphic example and confirmation of the ephemeral and transient nature of power and the futility of the vanity that goes with it. “What hit me even more was the fact that the Head of Protocol who spoke so loudly and aggressively on the day of our encounter and who said that if we did not allow the arms to be taken in they would fly Ghaddafi back home was one of those condemning him on CNN all the way from Paris on the day he was murdered”, he stated. The post How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish?
item.description: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish? Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match. That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February. Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust How many more points do Liverpool need for top-eight finish? At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game. That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home). The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare. That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton. Top-eight finish well within reach for Liverpool With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced. The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens. That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

item.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. The post Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’ appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Premier League form table updated ahead of 12th round of 2026-27 EPL matches
item.description: Brighton v Newcastle United This is how the Premier League form table looks ahead of the twelfth round of EPL matches, which include Brighton v Newcastle United. United having experienced a real game of two halves at St James’ Park against Arsenal last weekend. Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team are in action on Sunday. A 2.05pm kick-off at the Amex Stadium. Newcastle United looking to now follow up that excellent second half performance against the league leaders, with something similar against the club currently the nearest chasers to Arsenal. Premier League form table on Thursday 26 November 2026 The last six PL results for Newcastle United with very latest one listed first: Newcastle 2 Arsenal 2 Fulham 1 Newcastle 1 Newcastle 0 Everton 1 Palace 0 Newcastle 2 Newcastle 0 Villa 1 Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 As you can see, Newcastle United are sixteenth in this newly updated Premier League form table. In the Premier League form table over the last half dozen games, NUFC with five points from one win, two draws and three defeats, with six goals scored and nine conceded. As for Newcastle’s opponents on Sunday, these are the last six PL matches that Brighton have played, the very most recent listed first: Hull 2 Brighton 0 Brighton 2 Brentford 0 Man City 0 Brighton 1 Liverpool 2 Brighton 0 Brighton 5 Palace 0 Sunderland 0 Brighton 2 So Brighton are fourth in the Premier League form table with 12 points from four wins, no draws and two defeats, scoring ten and conceding four. Premier League table on Thursday 26 November 2026 The full Premier League table showing Brighton second top on 22 points, now six points behind leaders Arsenal. The Seagulls are 11 places and nine points ahead of Newcastle United . With only three points separating 13th place Newcastle with Chelsea in 8th, only five points between United and Bournemouth in 5th, a run of positive results against Brighton, Man U and Sunderland in the upcoming eight day run of games could potentially see a very different outlook. Though of course things can also go the other way… 🎙️ THE MAG PODCAST The Mag Pod Cover Ep 19: Newcastle 2–2 Arsenal, Bruno’s return and the games we missed Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! The Seagulls are 11 places and nine points ahead of Newcastle United . With only three points separating 13th place Newcastle with Chelsea in 8th, only five points between United and Bournemouth in 5th, a run of positive results against Brighton, Man U and Sunderland in the upcoming eight day run of games could potentially see a very different outlook. Though of course things can also go the other way… 🎙️ THE MAG PODCAST The Mag Pod Cover Ep 19: Newcastle 2–2 Arsenal, Bruno’s return and the games we missed Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! item.title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series
item.description: Inter Miami CF v D.C. United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. While the 2026 World Cup break allowed MLS to push the start of this year's play-offs past the international window, the gap from Decision Day to the quarter-finals still stretched to 28 days. The league had also weighed an Australian rules football-inspired double-elimination model before settling on its latest plan. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. "Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season," a spokesperson said at the time. A bid to restore regular-season intensity A primary driver behind the constant adjustments is the desire to raise the stakes of the regular season. Currently, 60 per cent of clubs qualify for the play-offs, creating an overly forgiving race. That leniency was highlighted this year when Real Salt Lake reached the first round despite winning just once in 16 matches after the World Cup. They edged out Minnesota United on Decision Day, even though Minnesota had endured a run of one victory in 18 games. The 2027-28 model will become the sixth different play-off format MLS has used since its 1996 launch. The league briefly abandoned multi-legged ties in 2019 before reintroducing extended series following its broadcast partnership with Apple, partly to guarantee lower-ranked qualifiers at least one match of post-season revenue. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. For now, clubs must navigate the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs under the existing system before the overhaul arrives alongside the league's new competition calendar in 2027-28. Some finer details of the revamped format still require clarification. It remains unknown how hosting order for the two-legged ties will be assigned, although the last MLS format to use home-and-away series gave the higher seed home advantage for the decisive second leg.

item.title: ‘Spiraling’ Final Trailer: Toni Tones Has Everything to Lose in Nigerian Thriller Series, Debuting on KAVA Today!
item.description: The four-part series, also starring Jim Iyke , Seun Ajayi and Folu Storms , is now streaming exclusively on KAVA . An illicit affair threatens to upend the life of a successful tech entrepreneur in the final trailer for Spiraling , the Nigerian psychological thriller from creator and director Wande Thomas , unveiled to coincide with the series’ streaming debut. Toni Tones ( King of Boys , The Smart Money Woman ) stars as Sade, a woman whose professional success and carefully curated personal life begin to unravel following a single lapse in judgment. Against the backdrop of a historic election, what starts as a private indiscretion escalates into a web of deception, betrayal and unprecedented consequences. Jim Iyke ( Bad Comments , Merry Men 2 ), Seun Ajayi ( Japa , The Smart Money Woman ) and Folu Storms ( Red Circle , Baby Farm ) round out the principal cast. A new series of character posters has also been released alongside the final trailer, spotlighting the key players in the psychological thriller. Exploring the intersection of ambition, desire and power, the series examines the lengths people will go to protect their reputations, and what happens when they can no longer control the narrative. Spiraling is created and directed by Thomas, who also produces alongside Isoken Ogiemwonyi under their respective production banners, Urbangidi Showtime and Studio Ogiso . The four-part thriller marks the latest addition to KAVA’s growing slate of straight to series African scripted entertainment. Watch the final trailer and see the newly released character posters below: More character posters here All four episodes of Spiraling are now streaming exclusively on KAVA. item.title: Champions League power rankings: Real Madrid surge – while rivals hit by injuries
item.description: Real Madrid will head to Arsenal in matchweek six of the Champions League with the only 100 per cent record remaining in the competition after Jose Mourinho’s side made it five wins from from five this season. The 15-time winners have found form just as a couple of their main rivals have been dealt major injury blows, too, with Bayern Munich ’s Harry Kane suffering an ankle injury and Paris Saint-Germain losing Desire Doue to an ACL injury, adding to the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. It means that will back-to-back winners PSG remain top of our standings, the competition is looking rather open underneath them – as the league phase table begins to take shape and the fight for the top-eight and play-off places intensifies. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings after matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below. ↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City, 4-2 v Barcelona, 6-0 v Villarreal, 2-2 v Roma Fixtures: Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h) Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions have seen their star-studded attack devastated by the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, who are both likely to be out for the rest of the season due to ACL issues. While Ousmane Dembele remains, as well as a brilliant midfield three, Enrique will have his work cut out if PSG are to remain as dangerous and retain their title this season. They dropped points for the first time in the Champions League this season as Roma secured a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Dembele will be without Kvaratskhelia and Doue for the rest of the season (Reuters) ↔️ 2. Barcelona Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray, 2-4 v PSG, 3-0 v Aston Villa, 4-1 v Sabah Fixtures: Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h) Even with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha rested, the goals kept flying and a double from Anthony Gordon in the 4-1 win over Sabah made it 69 goals in 18 games in all competitions this season from Hansi Flick’s side. The LaLiga champions are well placed to finish the league phase as one of the top seeds for the knockout stages, but the big question remains how their defence will stand up against one of the top teams. Conceding four in defeat against PSG means there is still much to prove. Gordon scored twice for Barcelona against Sabah (Reuters) ↔️ 3. item.content:encoded: Real Madrid will head to Arsenal in matchweek six of the Champions League with the only 100 per cent record remaining in the competition after Jose Mourinho’s side made it five wins from from five this season. The 15-time winners have found form just as a couple of their main rivals have been dealt major injury blows, too, with Bayern Munich ’s Harry Kane suffering an ankle injury and Paris Saint-Germain losing Desire Doue to an ACL injury, adding to the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. It means that will back-to-back winners PSG remain top of our standings, the competition is looking rather open underneath them – as the league phase table begins to take shape and the fight for the top-eight and play-off places intensifies. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings after matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below. ↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City, 4-2 v Barcelona, 6-0 v Villarreal, 2-2 v Roma Fixtures: Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h) Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions have seen their star-studded attack devastated by the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, who are both likely to be out for the rest of the season due to ACL issues. While Ousmane Dembele remains, as well as a brilliant midfield three, Enrique will have his work cut out if PSG are to remain as dangerous and retain their title this season. They dropped points for the first time in the Champions League this season as Roma secured a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Dembele will be without Kvaratskhelia and Doue for the rest of the season (Reuters) ↔️ 2. Barcelona Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray, 2-4 v PSG, 3-0 v Aston Villa, 4-1 v Sabah Fixtures: Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h) Even with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha rested, the goals kept flying and a double from Anthony Gordon in the 4-1 win over Sabah made it 69 goals in 18 games in all competitions this season from Hansi Flick’s side. The LaLiga champions are well placed to finish the league phase as one of the top seeds for the knockout stages, but the big question remains how their defence will stand up against one of the top teams. Conceding four in defeat against PSG means there is still much to prove. Gordon scored twice for Barcelona against Sabah (Reuters) ↔️ 3. Arsenal Results: 1-0 vs Napoli, 3-0 v Lille, 2-2 v Bayern Munich, 2-1 v Slavia Prague, 1-1 v Borussia Dortmund Fixtures: Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h) The arrival of winter is perhaps leading to some frustration, particularly in front of goal . Arsenal remain unbeaten but they were punished for not taking their opportunities as they dropped points at home to Borussia Dortmund, a result which means their place in the top-eight is not assured yet ahead of tough games against Real Madrid and Real Betis. Viktor Gyokeres was on target against Dortmund but Arsenal dropped points (Getty) ⬆️🟢 4. Real Madrid (+2 from 6) Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan, 4-3 v Roma, 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 3-2 v AEK Athens, 5-1 v PSV Fixtures: Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a) Real Madrid have come into a remarkable run of form, with a thumping win over PSV making it 10 wins in a row in all competitions under Jose Mourinho. It’s funny, in the Champions League, Real Madrid have trailed several games yet have maximum points. Now, the 15-time Champions League winners are not just managing to find a way, but they are blowing teams off the park. Jude Bellingham scored a brilliant volley in their big win over PSV (Getty) ⬆️🟢 5. Liverpool (+2 from 7) Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid, 6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal, 2-3 v Fenerbahce, 3-0 Club Brugge Fixtures: Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h) Before Andoni Iraola’s first season, it felt like so much depended on the potential of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz coming good in the Liverpool attack. Well, the signs of the past few weeks have been hugely promising as Isak and Wirtz continued to build their partnership in the 3-0 win at Club Brugge, with the Reds bouncing back from their shock defeat at Fenerbahce last time out. Florian Wirtz got on the scoresheet again in Belgium (Getty) ⬇️🔴 6. Bayern Munich (-2 from 4) Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt, 3-3 v Viking, 2-2 v Arsenal, 2-0 v Atletico Madrid, 1-2 v Lille Fixtures: Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h) The major concern for the German champions is the fitness of their Ballon d’Or holder Harry Kane, who will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury. Bayern have plenty of games to play until then and the question is whether they can get through to the top eight without Kane to avoid an additional play-off round. A stunning 2-1 defeat at Lille, which featured some calamitous defending and a truly remarkable Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal (honestly, go and check it out ...), saw Bayern drop to 15th in the table. Kane will be out until the knockout stages of the Champions League (Getty) ⬇️🔴 7. Man City (-2 from 5) Results: 2-0 v Porto, 2-4 v PSG, 5-1 v AEK Athens, 3-2 v Leipzig, 2-2 v Napoli Fixtures: Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a) Three defeats from four in the Premier League have well and truly taken shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well . After another sloppy performance against Napoli and the returning Kevin De Bruyne means it is now 10 games in a row without a clean sheet. City now face a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona and likely require a result to avoid dropping out of the top eight. Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli (PA) ⬆️🟢 8. Como (+2 from 10) Results: 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 2-3 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Manchester United, 9-1 v Lens, 1-0 v AEK Athens Fixtures: Real Betis (a), Paris Saint Germain (h), Barcelona (a) Up at the top of the table with the likes of Real Madrid, PSG and Barcelona, the Champions League debutants are certainly making a name for themselves. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side didn’t quite hit the same heights against AEK Athens after their nine-goal dismantling of poor Lens, but look what comes next. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase, after a tricky trip to Real Betis, are going to be fascinating. Como have four wins from their first five Champions League games, scoring 20 goals (Getty) ↔️ 9. Inter Milan Results: 1-2 v Real Madrid, 3-4 v Club Brugge, 1-0 v Shakhtar, 3-0 v Feyenoord, 2-0 v Stuttgart Fixtures: Borussia Dortmund (a), Liverpool (h), Slovan Bratislava (a) After starting with back-to-back defeats, Inter have responded with three consecutive wins. There was more good news in the 2-0 win over Stuttgart as Lautaro Martinez marked his return from injury after a month on the sidelines with a goal. Lautaro Martinez celebrated his return from injury (Getty) ⬆️🟢 10. Roma (+5 from 15) Results: 1-1 v Fenerbahce, 3-4 v Real Madrid, 4-0 v Slovan Bratislava, 2-3 v Manchester United, 2-2 v Paris-Saint Germain Fixtures: Sporting (h), AEK Athens (a), Lille (h) Sure, they absolutely bottled it against Real Madrid and Manchester United, throwing away leads on both occasions. Sure, they’ve got five points from five games in the Champions League and sit outside the top 24 in the league table. But a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain continued Roma’s impressive season under Gian Piero Gasperini; they remain unbeaten in Serie A and now have a more favourable run of games in the Champions League. On performances alone, they’ve earned a place in our top 10. Donyell Malen scored Roma’s equaliser in Paris (Reuters) ↔️ 11 . Atletico Madrid ↔️ 12. Borussia Dortmund ↔️ 13. Real Betis ⬇️ 🔴 14. Aston Villa (-6) ⬇️ 🔴 15. Manchester United (-1) ↔️ 16. Sporting ⬆️ 🟢 17. Galatasaray (+2) ⬇️ 🔴 18. Stuttgart (-1) ⬇️ 🔴 19. Club Brugge (

item.title: Charles Barkley heaps praise on Deni Avdija, Blazers after NBA Cup upset over Spurs
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Charles Barkley heaps praise on Deni Avdija, Blazers after NBA Cup upset over Spurs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Charles Barkley has never been shy about his praise for Deni Avdija. The former NBA player had plenty of praise for the young forward after the Portland Trail Blazers beat the San Antonio Spurs 116-111 in NBA Cup group-stage action on Wednesday night. Barkley also appreciated Portland’s athleticism and offensive firepower after the upset. He then singled out Avdija, praising his aggressive approach and comparing him to former NBA star Drazen Petrovic. “This is a good team, man. They big, they’re athletic, and when you have two guys who can score,” Barkley said. “And that boy Avdija, let me tell you something — he is so aggressive offensively. I love… I said at halftime, Stojaković… not Stojaković, Dražen Petrović — like he reminds me of him. Like he going straight forward, you going to stop him?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “[ Deni Avdija ’s] not afraid of anything, he’s not afraid of the moment.” Charles Barkley is a big fan of Deni Avdija and the Blazers 🗣️ (via @ESPNNBA ) pic.twitter.com/4lQO6BaxK6 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 26, 2026 Barkley added that Avdija isn’t afraid to take shots or make mistakes, even when his attempts aren’t falling. He also questioned the Washington Wizards’ decision to let the forward go. “I’m just trying to figure out why the Wizards let him go. It just goes to show you a lot of these teams don’t know what the hell they’re doing,” Barkley said. Avdija backed up that praise with a strong performance against San Antonio. He finished with 33 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists, while Damian Lillard added 29 points and seven assists to help Portland secure the win. Avdija also delivered the decisive moment and banked in a three-pointer with 37.9 seconds remaining to give the Blazers a five-point cushion. This was not the first time Barkley compared Avdija to Petrovic. During the 2026 NBA playoffs , Barkley made a similar comparison while discussing Avdija’s aggressive scoring mentality. The win tightened the race in West Group C, with Portland, San Antonio, Golden State, and the Los Angeles Lakers all sitting at 2-1 with one game remaining in the group stage. item.title: Exeter not 'the finished article', says boss Taylor
item.description: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. "Also, we have to take into account how far opposition teams have to travel down to us, same for us when we go to Oldham and Crawley, all these teams away from home, not just the north but London-based as well. item.content:encoded: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. This isn't an easy place to come to but we've got to make sure our energy is in the right place on Saturday." All the latest Exeter City news

item.title: 19 Hillsdale County volleyball athletes earn all-league SCAA-East
item.description: ILLSDALE COUNTY — Hillsdale County volleyball programs dominated the Southern Central Athletic Association East Division postseason honors following the 2026 fall sports season, accounting for all four Dream Team selections and 19 all-conference honorees. Hillsdale Academy seniors Lucy Cote and Malorie-Kate Apel and Pittsford juniors Alexis Bryner and Karmin Butler earned SCAA Dream Team honors, while Pittsford head coach Jessica Butler was named the division’s coach of the year. Butler led the Wildcats to a 21-12 overall record, their best finish since 2022, and an appearance in the Division 4 district championship game. Bryner, Cote and Apel also earned all-region honors from the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association this fall. Hillsdale Academy earned six all-conference selections after finishing the season 23-9 and capturing its fourth consecutive district championship along with the division crown. Joining Cote and Apel with first-team honors was fellow senior Zoe Plemmons. Camden-Frontier junior Zailey Conroy rounded out Hillsdale County’s first-team selections. Local athletes accounted for six of the seven first-team honorees. Five more Hillsdale County athletes earned second-team honors, including Pittsford freshman Layla Bryner and sophomore Ellie Bump, Hillsdale Academy junior Abigail Kriesch and freshman Lucy Molenkamp and Camden-Frontier junior Alyssa Schroeder. Litchfield, Waldron and North Adams-Jerome were also represented among the honorable mention selections, with all six Hillsdale County programs competing in the division earning postseason recognition. Here’s a look at the complete 2026 SCAA East Division volleyball all-conference selections. item.title: A Thanksgiving thank you from your local sportswriter | Richards
item.description: It always seems like a great idea. “Alright, everybody, let’s go around the dinner table and each share what we’re thankful for.” On the surface, it’s a lighthearted icebreaker that brings family and friends together to commemorate the start of the holiday season. In practice, it’s a ruthless mind game that feeds on the social anxieties lying beneath our cheerful exteriors. “Family,” the first person says, a layup. The next in line follows suit with another gimme, “Friends.” By this point, the wholesome answers have come to an end, and the jokes start rolling in. “This big ol’ turkey,” the third person chimes in, prompting a chuckle from the other participants in the annual ritual. When it reaches the fourth person, a nervous response follows: “All of this yummy food,” they say. At this point, family, friends and food are off the table. The big three have already been swooped up and we’re only through four people. Obviously, there’s no repeating. It’s the unspoken rule that everyone knows. I’m next. Of course there’s plenty to be thankful for, but at a moment like this nothing comes to mind. All I can hear is a single question racing through my head like static on a dead television channel — “What am I thankful for?” Fortunately, this year, I already know my answer. Three months ago, I started my job as the sports editor for The Daily Telegram in Adrian. It's been a whirlwind of a fall, and while I've spent plenty of time writing stories, compiling stats and emailing coaches, I haven't been able to properly acknowledge the people who have made the last three months possible. So, this Thanksgiving, I'd like to take a moment to do so on behalf of all local sportswriters. To athletic directors: Thank you for putting up with our copious amounts of emails. Keeping tabs on one sport is difficult enough, but overseeing numerous programs and hundreds of student-athletes makes you invaluable resources for writers and equally important figures in your respective schools. To coaches: Thank you for carving time out of your busy schedules to talk to us. For many of you, coaching comes on top of a full-time job as a teacher. Despite the demands on your time, you remain committed role models to your athletes, teaching lessons that extend well beyond the playing field. To student-athletes: Thank you for sharing your stories. Whether it's a quick postgame interview or a longer conversation about your journey, you give us stories worth telling. Your willingness to let us share a small piece of your lives with the community is something writers don't take for granted. And lastly, to our readers: Thank you for supporting local sports coverage. In a world increasingly dominated by algorithms, artificial intelligence and fleeting social media posts, you still make time for stories on those in your community. Whether through the mail slot or on your screens, you welcome our work into your homes. And in doing so, you remind us that there's still value in telling human s

item.title: Pochettino claims officials ‘punished’ Manchester United in chaotic Sporting draw
item.description: Head coach questions ‘difficult to understand’ decisions Zirkzee joins Pochettino in offering support to Lammens Mauricio Pochettino claimed Manchester United were punished unfairly after again appearing to suffer from faulty officiating in Wednesday night’s 2-2 draw at Sporting. The key decision from Szymon Marciniak came when Amad Diallo’s first-half strike was ruled out due to the referee adjudging Youri Tielemans to have fouled Gonçalo Inácio just before the finish. Tielemans was booked and so when he received a second yellow card in second-half added time, he was sent off for United’s fifth red card in their last nine games. This followed Leny Yoro’s red card in Sunday’s 4-0 loss at Liverpool that was later rescinded. Continue reading...

item.title: Oliver Bearman locks in Haas F1 seat as 2027 grid officially set
item.description: Motorsport photo Oliver Bearman will officially stay at Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season after he and the team finally put pen to paper on a new deal. The American squad announced the renewal on Thursday, meaning the 21-year-old Briton will partner Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara at Haas next season. It means the 2027 grid is now complete ahead of the final two rounds of the 2026 campaign, one in which Bearman has shone with 23 of Haas' 31 points. Team boss Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us. "We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. "He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward. Ayao Komatsu, Haas Ayao Komatsu, Haas "TGR Haas F1 Team has one of the most exciting driver pairings on the grid, and I look forward to seeing Ollie flourish further with this incredible team." Next season will be Bearman's third, full campaign in F1, although he did make three appearances in 2024 - his debut for Ferrari in Jeddah, before outings in Baku and Sao Paulo for Haas. "It’s no secret that I’m delighted to be continuing with TGR Haas F1 Team into 2027," said Bearman. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. "We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business." Although this news comes late into the season, the Ferrari protege was always going to stay with Haas, which has loaned him from the Scuderia since his rookie year. Oliver Bearman, Haas Oliver Bearman, Haas But as he is entering year three with the American squad, Bearman's camp also wanted assurances about his long-term future - with driving for Ferrari being his ultimate goal. Bearman's camp is also believed to have been looking for a significant pay increase, considering he's become Haas' lead driver after outperforming the now ousted Esteban Ocon . At last week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman admitted he was "quite disappointed" that "I'm sitting here at round 20 without a contract signed for next year. It's been a strange situation, but we're getting there." He now heads into Qatar this weekend with that new deal ahead of the Abu Dhabi finale, as Haas attempts to hold off Audi in the battle for seventh with three points separating them. item.title: 20 Years Later, One of TV’s Greatest Sci-Fi Franchises Still Hasn’t Topped Its Riskiest Spin-Off
item.description: Last year was a mixed bag for Whovians. Disney dumped Doctor Who , leaving the franchise in such dire straits that the BBC had no choice but to look for someone new to steer the long-running sci-fi show into a new era. That said, the franchise also got a major win with Russell T. Davies and director Dylan Holmes-Williams’s climate-focused spin-off, The War Between Land and Sea , which debuted in the U.K. that December but still hasn't officially been released in the U.S.

item.title: AI solved the hardest problem in maths – is there anything it can’t do?
item.description: Alzheimer’s disease, involving amyloid plaques in the brain, will be tough for AI to solve JUAN GAERTNER/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY The progress AI has made in mathematics this year is nothing short of extraordinary. In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths . The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. Read more Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name. Biology is a big one. “Cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness – these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei while promoting the company’s recent initial public offering . “I think one day maybe we can cure all disease with the help of AI,” said Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, last year , adding that this could be “within the next decade or so”. This phenomenon isn’t new: I call it “physicist brain”, after the propensity for physicists to wade into areas outside their expertise and declare simple solutions. More broadly, it is called Nobel disease , after the many Nobel prizewinners who have gone on to make, shall we say, less evidenced-backed claims. In general, there is a tendency to think that if an intelligent person is good at one thing, they are good at many other things that require intelligence. What is different now is that trillion-dollar companies and large swathes of the global economy now depend on this being true of artificial intelligence. Advertisement To be clear, I think we must now admit that AI is better at solving open mathematical problems than any human, and that this has happened faster than anyone ever expected. When I first saw the news in September that the Navier-Stokes problem had been solved by OpenAI , I felt stunned. We had entered a new world. With the announcement of the Riemann hypothesis proof this week, I felt sick and had to go and have a lie-down. These were intellectual Everests I have marvelled at since my teenage years, conquered by a machine far sooner than anyone expected. You may have read my recent piece forecasting the future in 2096 – an early draft had a line, later removed, about three Millennium Prize Problems being solved by AI in the 2030s. We’ve had two this year alone. But maths isn’t biology. Yes, we have seen advances like AlphaFold, Deepmind’s AI that can predict the structure of proteins , but this is biology at its most mathematical, a computational puzzle. True advances in biology and medicine require studying cells, animals and people, all of which can be frustratingly illogical and uncooperative. item.content:encoded: Alzheimer’s disease, involving amyloid plaques in the brain, will be tough for AI to solve JUAN GAERTNER/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY The progress AI has made in mathematics this year is nothing short of extraordinary. In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths . The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. Read more Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name. Biology is a big one. “Cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness – these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei while promoting the company’s recent initial public offering . “I think one day maybe we can cure all disease with the help of AI,” said Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, last year , adding that this could be “within the next decade or so”. This phenomenon isn’t new: I call it “physicist brain”, after the propensity for physicists to wade into areas outside their expertise and declare simple solutions. More broadly, it is called Nobel disease , after the many Nobel prizewinners who have gone on to make, shall we say, less evidenced-backed claims. In general, there is a tendency to think that if an intelligent person is good at one thing, they are good at many other things that require intelligence. What is different now is that trillion-dollar companies and large swathes of the global economy now depend on this being true of artificial intelligence. Advertisement To be clear, I think we must now admit that AI is better at solving open mathematical problems than any human, and that this has happened faster than anyone ever expected. When I first saw the news in September that the Navier-Stokes problem had been solved by OpenAI , I felt stunned. We had entered a new world. With the announcement of the Riemann hypothesis proof this week, I felt sick and had to go and have a lie-down. These were intellectual Everests I have marvelled at since my teenage years, conquered by a machine far sooner than anyone expected. You may have read my recent piece forecasting the future in 2096 – an early draft had a line, later removed, about three Millennium Prize Problems being solved by AI in the 2030s. We’ve had two this year alone. But maths isn’t biology. Yes, we have seen advances like AlphaFold, Deepmind’s AI that can predict the structure of proteins , but this is biology at its most mathematical, a computational puzzle. True advances in biology and medicine require studying cells, animals and people, all of which can be frustratingly illogical and uncooperative. Amodei admitted as much in 2024, writing that “the main challenges with directly applying intelligence to biology are data, the speed of the physical world, and intrinsic complexity”. You can imagine mitigations here – AI-directed robotic labs, for example – but it doesn’t seem like we should expect massive speed leaps in capability comparable to those seen in mathematics. There isn’t an easy way to confirm that a biological discovery is correct, in the manner that the computer code Lean allows for mathematics . Worse still are claims that AI will “solve climate change”. For Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, this came as a throwaway comment in a 2024 essay : “Although it will happen incrementally, astounding triumphs – fixing the climate, establishing a space colony, and the discovery of all of physics – will eventually become commonplace.” But we already know the solution to climate change: reduce greenhouse gas emissions to net zero and the warming will stop. The blockers to doing so, as demonstrated by the recent failure of the COP31 climate summit , are political, not technological. Even if AI were to produce a blueprint for a perfectly functioning nuclear fusion reactor tomorrow, we would still have to build thousands of them across the globe in the next decade or so to avoid the most catastrophic warming effects. In the past decade, we have built 60 nuclear fission reactors , a technology we understand far better than an as-yet-mythical fusion power plant. Again, you can see how AI might offer some improvements, but not enough to counteract our fossil fuel use. It is important for me to have some humility here, because one thing AI’s breakthroughs in mathematics this year has underlined for me is the need to change my mind when the evidence changes. I started that process with the early signs of AI progress in maths, but didn’t update my beliefs fast enough – though, to be fair to myself, neither did almost everyone else, including leading mathematicians such as Terence Tao, who, just weeks ago, said he didn’t expect the Riemann hypothesis to be solved by AI until 2050 . For that reason, I am on the lookout for early signs that AI success in biology is shifting. That could include an AI-designed drug proving useful in people – for example, Rentosertib , a leading candidate, is now undergoing a phase III trial as a treatment for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a type of lung disease. The trial is expected to conclude in 2029 , so we’re talking years of wait for any results. If the drug succeeds, that doesn’t necessarily provide a way for any other AI drug candidates to succeed, and the painfully slow process of molecule selection, animal testing and human trials is still hard to speed up. If I’m forced to make a prediction, I can fairly confidently state that we will see yet more advances in AI maths in 2027. I also expect that we will see some completely unexpected results in other fields as well. But solving biology? Ending climate change? Defeating disease? These still feel, for now, like science fiction. Read more AI refutes 30-year-old mathematical assumption in computer science Further AI reading AI maths has become a spectator sport, thanks to a website dedicated to tracking agents attempting to solve the P vs NP problem , one of the remaining huge open problems in mathematics ( see my explanation of it here ). I don’t expect this approach to work – the models being used here are consumer ones, rather than the internal frontier models the AI firms have used for the big maths results so far. As if to illustrate this, both OpenAI and Anthropic have released, with little fanfare, solutions to the VP vs VNP problem . This is a lesser version of the P vs NP problem, and doesn’t necessarily help us get any closer to solving its big brother. And speaking of internal models, Axios reports that both Anthropic and OpenAI employees are concerned that their internal models are so powerful that they can’t safely be released . Take this with a big pinch of salt – Anthropic said the same about its Mythos model due to its cybersecurity abilities , then later released its Fable model, which is essentially just Mythos with some added guardrails. And don’t forget that, way back in the mists of 2019, OpenAI said that GPT-2 would be too dangerous to release . Today, you can run far more capable models on a smartphone, and no one finds that dangerous. Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after a mere 11 days away following a scandal about his admitted affair with an alleged Chinese spy. For a reminder of why Nvidia is so important to the AI industry, see my previous column . A UN conference has failed to agree to a ban on autonomous weapons, as my colleague Matthew Sparkes predicted last week .

item.title: 2027: ADC’s Babba Kaita Rallies Katsina Voters, Promises LG Autonomy, Anti-Corruption Drive
item.description: The Katsina State Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 general elections, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita, has described the forthcoming polls as a crucial battle that Nigerians must pursue with determination and collective strength. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. The statement said residents, including youths, women and community leaders, have continued to welcome the campaign team with prayers, endorsements and assurances of support as the party intensifies its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. The post 2027: ADC’s Babba Kaita Rallies Katsina Voters, Promises LG Autonomy, Anti-Corruption Drive appeared first on Channels Television .
