item.title: New York Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade Over Major Storm
item.description: New York postponed the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday over fears of extreme weather, a first in the event’s 100-year history, as a major storm gathers steam on the US East Coast. The brewing “nor’easter” threatens to disrupt plans for millions of people hitting the road and flying around the Thursday holiday, one of the country’s busiest travel seasons. “With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s told AFP in a statement. A balloon of Buckaroo Bob The Minion rests under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP The date change has prompted questions about the thousands of parade participants, including musicians and technical staff, who had made arrangements for a Thursday parade. “Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday,” the company said. The annual parade sees brightly colored balloons travel some 2.5 miles (four kilometers) from Midtown Manhattan to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store on 34th Street. Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. It is the first time in its history that it has been postponed, The New York Post reported. ‘Heartbroken’ New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed press conference on November 25, 2026 in New York City. Manoli Figetakis/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Manoli Figetakis / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) “This will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour, with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a safety briefing Wednesday. “The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning as well as a coastal flood warning. “Winds will be strong enough (Thursday) to down tree limbs and power lines.” The worst of the storm will strike later Thursday when strong winds, heavy rain and the evening high tide will overlap, the city warned in a travel advisory. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade in 1997. Workers prepare a balloon under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP Volunteers struggled but failed to keep a tight rein on ropes which constantly threatened to slam into onlookers. item.title: 'We are not fighting culture, we fight to end FGM: It's a human rights violation of women and girls'
item.description: “We fight to end FGM because it is a human rights violation of women and girls. We are not fighting culture.” Caroline Lagat, Legal Advisor at Equality Now’s Africa office in Nairobi, discusses the challenges of ending female genital mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. She points to insufficient funding, conflicting marriage laws and growing community resistance to campaigns against FGM. While acknowledging some progress, Lagat calls on the government to be "the face of the campaign to end FGM and child marriage.”

item.title: #EndSARS: Court gives hospital 14 days to release Onifade’s remains
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State District Coroner, Mrs Temitope Oladele, has ordered the Infectious Diseases Hospital (IDH), Yaba, Lagos, to release the remains of late journalist, Pelumi Onifade, to his parents within 14 days for burial. The order was issued during the ongoing inquest into the death of the Gboah TV reporter, who was reportedly shot during the #EndSARS protests in October 2020 and subsequently died in police custody. Oladele granted the application by the family’s counsel, Alimi Adamu, who also represents Media Rights Agenda, MRA, following six years of retention of the deceased’s remains at the hospital. The coroner directed that the remains, identified by tag number 1385, be released to the family within 14 days of the hospital receiving the order. The inquest also issued fresh witness summons to persons considered crucial to establishing the circumstances surrounding Onifade’s shooting, arrest and death. The proceedings followed a July 19, 2024 judgment of the Federal High Court in Lagos, which directed the Lagos State Attorney-General to investigate Onifade’s death, conduct a coroner’s inquest and identify and prosecute those responsible. At the latest sitting, Adamu told the court that efforts to secure the attendance of a witness reportedly present when Onifade was killed had been unsuccessful. He said the witness could provide important evidence about the journalist’s arrest and subsequent disappearance but was apprehensive about appearing in court. Adamu urged the coroner to allow the witness to testify electronically, with measures to protect his identity. The court approved the application for the summons to be served through WhatsApp. Another witness, Jimmy Michael, reportedly with Onifade at the time of the shooting, was also summoned. Counsel to the Lagos State Attorney-General, Adebola Araba, told the court that Michael had explained that his Christmas business engagements prevented him from attending, but he had not refused to participate in the inquest. The court equally identified Gboah TV Director, Michael Oluwajoba Bamiro, as a relevant witness, approving his appearance at the next sitting. Onifade’s mother, Bose, also adopted her witness statement on oath, filed on November 11, 2026, which the court admitted in evidence. Adamu urged the coroner to record that the remains had been kept in state custody for forensic and judicial purposes to facilitate administrative arrangements, including issues relating to storage fees. The inquest was adjourned until December 15, 2026, for further proceedings. The post #EndSARS: Court gives hospital 14 days to release Onifade’s remains appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Protesters, FIFA boss, Democrat, spy: People who helped define 2026
item.description: Of the many people who made their mark on 2026, five in particular stand out — from an alleged Chinese spy to FIFA’s troubled president and a Madrid pensioner who became the face of Spain’s housing protests. – Alice Huang – She’s the woman at the heart of the international espionage scandal whose ripple effects are still emerging. Suspected of spying for Beijing, Alice Huang flew under the radar until the explosive revelation of her affair with the chief of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang. The outcry saw him resign, before being sensationally reinstated just days later after the intervention of US President Donald Trump. Alice Huang — no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen — is a former director of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia AI chips in violation of US export controls. China denies the spying allegations. Alice Huang has not been seen since the scandal erupted. Details on her life are murky, but the Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport was filmed at a Taipei party in 2025 wearing a pink dress as she kissed Jensen Huang on the cheek. His departure on November 12 tanked Nvidia’s market value, sparking infighting within the Trump administration over what officials knew, and raising the spectre of trade clashes with China as the US tightens export controls of advanced AI chips. Nvidia’s shares rose 30 percent after the tech giant announced on November 23 that it had reinstated Huang, with Trump saying he had spoken to the board “directly”, igniting a political backlash and leaving many questions unanswered. – Gianni Infantino – FIFA President Gianni Infantino oversaw a highly successful World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, even brushing off a controversial episode when USA forward Folarin Balogun had his red card suspended following a direct appeal by Trump. But football is a game of highs and lows, and within weeks Infantino faced calls to stand down over plans to sell stakes in World Cup commercial rights to a company run by the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. The proposal was hastily dropped following opposition led by European confederation UEFA, leaving Infantino’s re-election plans in March 2027 in peril. French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo was UEFA’s late choice as candidate. But he and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima face an uphill task to dislodge Infantino, who has been backed by the Asian, African and South American football federations. – Abdul El-Sayed – Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate following a stunning victory in the race for the Michigan seat during November’s midterm elections. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said of his win, one of many on a seismic night for his party. The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises while Republicans branded the straight-talking 42-year-old a terrorist who would endanger Americans

Suspected of spying for Beijing, Alice Huang flew under the radar until the explosive revelation of her affair with the chief of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang. The outcry saw him resign, before being sensationally reinstated just days later after the intervention of US President Donald Trump. Alice Huang — no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen — is a former director of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia AI chips in violation of US export controls. China denies the spying allegations. Alice Huang has not been seen since the scandal erupted. Details on her life are murky, but the Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport was filmed at a Taipei party in 2025 wearing a pink dress as she kissed Jensen Huang on the cheek. His departure on November 12 tanked Nvidia’s market value, sparking infighting within the Trump administration over what officials knew, and raising the spectre of trade clashes with China as the US tightens export controls of advanced AI chips. Nvidia’s shares rose 30 percent after the tech giant announced on November 23 that it had reinstated Huang, with Trump saying he had spoken to the board “directly”, igniting a political backlash and leaving many questions unanswered. – Gianni Infantino – FIFA President Gianni Infantino oversaw a highly successful World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, even brushing off a controversial episode when USA forward Folarin Balogun had his red card suspended following a direct appeal by Trump. But football is a game of highs and lows, and within weeks Infantino faced calls to stand down over plans to sell stakes in World Cup commercial rights to a company run by the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. The proposal was hastily dropped following opposition led by European confederation UEFA, leaving Infantino’s re-election plans in March 2027 in peril. French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo was UEFA’s late choice as candidate. But he and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima face an uphill task to dislodge Infantino, who has been backed by the Asian, African and South American football federations. – Abdul El-Sayed – Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate following a stunning victory in the race for the Michigan seat during November’s midterm elections. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said of his win, one of many on a seismic night for his party. The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises while Republicans branded the straight-talking 42-year-old a terrorist who would endanger Americans. El-Sayed allied with left-leaning influencers and union activists, who lent their formidable campaign infrastructure to reach Michigan’s large organised labor community. He faced mockery for his Arabic name from Trump and Vice President JD Vance, but may yet have the last laugh. Addressing the vice president, El-Sayed said in his victory speech “you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January”. – Maricarmen – Lying on a stretcher, her face drawn, Maricarmen Abascal, 87, bade farewell to the home she had lived in for 70 years. The Madrid resident was evicted from her home on September 23 and became the face of Spain’s housing crisis, sparking nationwide protests that triggered a snap general election. Demonstrations and pot-banging protests spread across Spain, with camps set up in places like Madrid’s iconic Puerta del Sol square. The country fell into mourning when she died in hospital two weeks later. Abascal spent years fighting a legal battle against a property agency that bought her apartment and raised the monthly rent by 275 percent to 2,650 euros. “You cannot make someone live for seven years with a machete hanging over their head,” she said. – Abhijeet Dipke – For Abhijeet Dipke, 2026 was the year an internet joke made him the face of a youth movement. The communications strategist was in the US when a remark comparing unemployed youth to cockroaches prompted his May 16 post: “What if all cockroaches come together?” The 30-year-old went on to create the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical group which attracted millions of followers, surpassing even the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. It became a nationwide movement, mobilising thousands against medical entrance paper leaks, unemployment and government inaction. Dipke returned to India despite death threats to his family and fears of arrest. “I need to take a stand,” he told AFP in July. Protests eventually helped secure education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation in July, marking a rare climbdown for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government. CJP later turned to electoral reform, demanding the chief election commissioner’s resignation over an overhaul of voter lists they claim unfairly benefits the ruling party. The post Protesters, FIFA boss, Democrat, spy: People who helped define 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alero Ebigbeyi: Making a Case for Quality, Affordable Fashion with HÉYCH
item.description: After more than 30 years of experience in the fashion industry, the entrepreneur is bringing her experience to a Nigerian clothing brand built on a simple proposition: quality should not have to come at an exorbitant price. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. It was a response that reflected the thinking behind HÉYCH, a brand seeking to occupy an important space in the market by making well-made, stylish clothing accessible without asking consumers to compromise on quality. For Ebigbeyi, this approach is informed by more than three decades of experience in the fashion industry. Having spent over 30 years understanding the business of clothing, she brings to HÉYCH a perspective that extends beyond trends and aesthetics to the practical realities of production, pricing and delivering value. “One thing that sets HÉYCH apart is that we do not compromise on quality, and we are equally intentional about making our products affordable. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. Importation can introduce several layers of cost and complexity, from logistics and shipping to delays and quality-control challenges. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. It was a response that reflected the thinking behind HÉYCH, a brand seeking to occupy an important space in the market by making well-made, stylish clothing accessible without asking consumers to compromise on quality. For Ebigbeyi, this approach is informed by more than three decades of experience in the fashion industry. Having spent over 30 years understanding the business of clothing, she brings to HÉYCH a perspective that extends beyond trends and aesthetics to the practical realities of production, pricing and delivering value. “One thing that sets HÉYCH apart is that we do not compromise on quality, and we are equally intentional about making our products affordable. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. Importation can introduce several layers of cost and complexity, from logistics and shipping to delays and quality-control challenges. Producing locally offers an opportunity to reduce some of these constraints, exercise closer oversight of production and create a more direct relationship between the manufacturer and the customer. “Establishing our production facility here in Lagos is a deliberate business decision. Local manufacturing allows us to eliminate many of the bottlenecks associated with importing clothing, reduce unnecessary costs and maintain better control over the quality of what we produce. We want our customers to enjoy excellent products without having to pay unnecessarily high prices,” she explains. It is an approach that also gives HÉYCH a broader commercial outlook. Beyond individual retail customers, the brand is positioning its production capacity to serve churches, concert organisers, corporate organisations, event producers and other brands that require clothing in substantial quantities. For these clients, working with a local manufacturer can offer greater flexibility, closer communication and the opportunity to carry out quality checks during production. It also creates an alternative to sourcing large clothing orders from overseas markets, particularly when customisation, timelines and consistency are important. Fashion, Business and the Value of Local Enterprise There is a larger conversation taking place around Nigeria’s fashion industry, particularly the need to strengthen local production and create more opportunities within the country’s creative and manufacturing sectors. While Nigerian designers and fashion brands have earned recognition for their creativity, the infrastructure required to support production at scale remains an important part of the industry’s development. HÉYCH’s model brings this conversation into focus by connecting retail fashion with manufacturing capacity. The benefits also extend beyond the products themselves. Local production creates employment opportunities and supports the people and processes involved in turning clothing concepts into finished products. For Ebigbeyi, building HÉYCH is therefore about creating a business that can deliver commercial value while contributing to the local economy. This is perhaps what makes the brand’s proposition interesting. It is not simply about encouraging consumers to buy Nigerian-made clothing; it is about demonstrating that locally produced fashion can be commercially competitive, quality-conscious and accessible. A Brand with More Than One Ambition The opening of the HÉYCH retail store marks an important step in introducing the brand to a wider audience, but its ambitions extend beyond the retail experience. By combining a consumer-facing fashion offering with the capacity for large-scale production, the brand is exploring two connected opportunities within the Nigerian market. For Ebigbeyi, the direction is clear: build a brand that understands what customers want, respects the importance of quality and recognises that affordability must be part of the equation. With more than 30 years of industry experience informing its direction, HÉYCH enters the market with a proposition that speaks to both the everyday fashion consumer and organisations looking for a dependable local clothing production partner. Ultimately, its story is part of a wider question about the future of Nigerian fashion: how can the industry move beyond creativity to build stronger production capabilities, create jobs and make quality clothing more accessible? For Alero Ebigbeyi, HÉYCH is one answer to that question. About HÉYCH HÉYCH is a Nigerian fashion and clothing brand committed to delivering quality, style and affordability through locally driven production. With a retail store and manufacturing facility in Lagos, the brand serves individual customers, institutions, corporate organisations, churches, concert organisers and other clients requiring clothing in large quantities. Visit our store at 28B Abike Sulaiman Street, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos, and explore our fabulous collection. There’s something beautiful waiting for you. Shop HÉYCH. Wear confidence. Own your style. Follow us at @theheych for more updates and style inspiration. item.title: Kerrygold Brings Milk & Magic Christmas Fest to Lagos This December
item.description: Christmas is a time for making memories, sharing special moments and enjoying the little things that make the season memorable. This December, Kerrygold is bringing some extra magic to the festive season with its Milk & Magic Christmas Fest , a free family-friendly celebration of food, fun and togetherness. Scheduled for Saturday, 5 December 2026, at Ikeja City Mall, Lagos, the festival promises a day filled with exciting activities and festive experiences for children and adults alike. Families can look forward to a fun-filled day out, with free admission upon registration, making it a lovely opportunity to step away from their usual routines and create special memories together. From exciting games and interactive activities to the much-loved Santa’s Grotto, there will be plenty to keep guests entertained. Children can look forward to the magic and excitement of the season, while parents get to enjoy the experience alongside them. And, of course, no celebration would be complete without a little indulgence. Guests can also look forward to delicious milk treats from Kerrygold, adding a taste of the brand to the day’s festivities. Beyond the fun and entertainment, Milk & Magic Christmas Fest reflects Kerrygold’s commitment to creating meaningful connections with consumers beyond the products they enjoy every day. By bringing families together in a relaxed and engaging setting, the festival offers an opportunity to experience the brand in a different way, while celebrating the simple pleasures of good food and shared moments. With its distinctive rich, creamy taste and proud Irish dairy heritage, Kerrygold continues to bring quality dairy experiences closer to Nigerian consumers. Through its products and consumer engagement initiatives, the brand remains focused on creating experiences that resonate with its consumers and bring people together. As the countdown to Christmas begins, Milk & Magic Christmas Fest promises a lovely opportunity for families to share in the excitement of the season, enjoy some festive treats and make memories that will last beyond the holidays. Would you love to enjoy this festive experience with your family? Admission is FREE, but registration is required and spaces are limited. Visit https://milkandmagicfest.com/ to register now! item.title: Iyabo Ojo apologises over viral handshake video
item.description: Nollywood actress, Iyabo Ojo, has apologised following a viral video showing a man appearing to decline her handshake at an event, explaining that she was unaware he was a traditional ruler. The actress addressed the controversy in a statement posted on her Instagram page, saying she had approached the table after being informed that some people seated there had sent greetings to her. Ojo said she recognised HRM Oloto, whom she described as her brother, and assumed the other people at the table were his friends. “I was sitting pretty when someone came to tell me they sent their greetings from that table. When I looked in that direction and saw HRM Oloto, I said, ‘Ah, okay, that’s my brother, let me go greet him,’” she said. “Honestly, I am very sorry if I caused any offence. I meant no disrespect to his throne and culture. Henceforth, I will be very mindful,” she stated. Ojo also acknowledged that she was accustomed to greeting people with handshakes and hugs, noting that she had been making efforts to change the habit. “We learn every day. I meant no disrespect. It’s all love from this side,” she added. The post Iyabo Ojo apologises over viral handshake video appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US lists 63 professions eligible for 3-year work visa
item.description: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. Canadian citizens can generally apply for TN status at a US port of entry or designated pre-clearance facility without first obtaining a TN visa from a US embassy. Mexican citizens, however, must obtain a TN nonimmigrant visa from a US embassy or consulate before seeking admission into the country. The arrangement was originally introduced under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which came into force in 1994. It was retained when the USMCA replaced NAFTA on July 1, 2020. item.content:encoded: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. Canadian citizens can generally apply for TN status at a US port of entry or designated pre-clearance facility without first obtaining a TN visa from a US embassy. Mexican citizens, however, must obtain a TN nonimmigrant visa from a US embassy or consulate before seeking admission into the country. The arrangement was originally introduced under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which came into force in 1994. It was retained when the USMCA replaced NAFTA on July 1, 2020. Despite the professional opportunities it provides, the TN classification is not open to citizens of other countries. This means that Nigerians and other foreign nationals cannot qualify for the arrangement solely because they possess the required professional qualifications or have secured employment in one of the listed occupations. The US Department of State specifically states that permanent residents of Canada and Mexico are also ineligible, as applicants must hold citizenship of either country. The TN arrangement therefore remains a specialised employment route designed to facilitate professional mobility among the three North American trade partners. item.title: ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start
item.description: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino insisted his team would find a way to win games after a tricky start to life at the helm of the Red Devils. United were held to a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, after a 4-0 thrashing by rivals Liverpool in his first match on Sunday. Man United, 19th in the Premier League, were upset with several refereeing decisions across both matches, but Pochettino said his team had to take responsibility for their situation. “I’m happy to be here,” said Pochettino, when asked about the various decisions that had gone against his team in his first week in charge. “We are here to take responsibility… we are going for sure to improve and to put that team in the place that, because of their history, we deserve to be. “Nothing is easy but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and most importantly the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive and I think united, all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.” United had two goals controversially ruled out against Sporting, but might have won the game were it not for a mistake from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Belgian dropped the ball for Colombian striker Luis Suarez to score his second goal of the night, cancelling out Bruno Fernandes’s double against his old side. Lammens also saved a Suarez penalty and then gave away a second penalty, this time scored by the striker. “This type of thing happens, that is football,” said Pochettino. “Football is about making mistakes — I’m going to support always my player if something happens.” The Argentine said Man United’s defenders might have done better to help protect Lammens before he spilled the ball. “When you are a ‘keeper, it’s not easy, that ball. And always you need help from your teammates,” added Pochettino. “But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve in all the small details that for sure we will improve.” The post ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: No drums, no tifo … no point? The impact of Palace’s missing Holmesdale Fanatics
item.description: Crystal Palace’s influential supporters’ group disbanded 24 hours before their first home game this season – and Selhurst Park has not been the same since Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket. “Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.” Continue reading...

item.title: Dangote Refinery shares to trade on NGX December 1
item.description: Shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) on December 1, the company has announced. Devakumar Edwin, Vice-President, Oil and Gas, Dangote Group, disclosed the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing will follow the refinery’s initial public offering (IPO), which attracted significant investor interest and was heavily oversubscribed. The development comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s plan to allocate shares to investors, paving the way for the completion of the offer and its stock market debut. Dangote Refinery had sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong demand from investors. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, President of Dangote Industries Limited, said the refinery planned to list on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, the industrialist said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and other parts of the world. The post Dangote Refinery shares to trade on NGX December 1 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Aid cuts to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further curb women's access to healthcare, education and food
item.description: Having lived and worked in Afghanistan for seven years, photojournalist Élise Blanchard offers an intimate account of what daily life is like for Afghan women today. Joining Genie Godula on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, she explains how restrictions vary across the country, depending on where women live, their families and the local enforcement of Taliban decrees. She stresses the need to maintain access to healthcare, primary education and food, pointing to severe cuts in humanitarian assistance by the US and EU.

item.title: Registered Voters Now 100m As INEC Removes 1.6m Invalid Records
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The update comes as the Commission said it has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. According to him, the Commission removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register – the removal has now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were taken off the list, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. “Beyond hardware and logistics, we must also account for inclusivity and evidentiary clarity. Following three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) that added over 10.77 million new registrants and an ABIS and statutory claims-and-objections audit that purged over 1.6 million invalid, duplicate, or deceased records, our verified register stands at over 100 million citizens, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) requiring accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were an additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. item.dc:creator: OpeOluwani Akintayo
item.content:encoded: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The update comes as the Commission said it has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. According to him, the Commission removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register – the removal has now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were taken off the list, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. “Beyond hardware and logistics, we must also account for inclusivity and evidentiary clarity. Following three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) that added over 10.77 million new registrants and an ABIS and statutory claims-and-objections audit that purged over 1.6 million invalid, duplicate, or deceased records, our verified register stands at over 100 million citizens, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) requiring accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were an additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. He said that although INEC had previously stood down its broader revalidation exercise until after the elections, the commission resolved to immediately address serious infractions identified on the old register. “So, consequent upon that, the ICT department, working with the Voter Registry, have been able to complete the validation of those that contain duplications only, and those we had some form of stroke registrations. “In other words, those places where you have BBBB, AAAA, CCCC without complete names, we felt that those ones are too serious to be left on the old register. “So, where you also have duplication, one name, same picture, having five registrations, we have also addressed all those numbers. “By the time we are putting the verified and clean-up register together, the national voters’ register is reduced from 103 million to 100 million,’’ Amupitan said. He added that the Commission has deployed 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices across the country, and is coordinating over 1.41 million ad hoc election personnel across diverse terrains—from dense urban centres to remote riverine communities, insurgency-affected corridors, and locations hosting internally displaced persons. item.title: The defence tech revolution is changing how we innovate
item.description: Cpl Aaron J Stone/UK Ministry of Defence Only five years ago, defence technology start-ups had little choice but to wait for government funding to build and test their inventions – often in complex, multi-year programmes. No longer, however: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has prompted such a fast, furious response that military innovation timescales have shrunk dramatically. “Ukraine is becoming a real-world lab for military innovation, and it’s innovating at a pace greater than anything that we’ve seen previously,” says Ola Fashade, an air vice-marshal in the Royal Air Force and director of military digitalisation and the rapid AI delivery task force at the UK’s Ministry of Defence (MoD). “Agility and tempo of adaptation is critical. In a contested battlespace, technology that works well on day one, by day eight has become a little muted – and by day twelve it’s probably no longer relevant. And if you don’t adapt over that period, what you have is a very expensive and ineffective bag of steel.” Advertisement That raises the question of how significant this accelerated innovation could become. In September 2026, New Scientist CoLab, sponsored by BAE Systems, brought together leading thinkers and investors from industry, the military and academia to discuss the factors driving this innovation and the lessons that can be transferred to other industries. Staying alive The investment for this step change is coming both from the technology incubators based within military prime contractors – like the Launchpad incubator at BAE Systems – and from a host of venture capital (VC) companies worldwide. “The idea behind Launchpad is to forge an ecosystem that gets technology from defence start-ups into the front line quicker, or into spinouts, before they run out of money and die,” says David Ewing, head of technology commercialisation at BAE Systems. In addition, VC funding is seeing a raft of new multibillion-dollar military tech players, dubbed neoprimes, that complement the work of the primes on bigger-ticket battlespace items. The poster child for the neoprimes, says Samuel Burrell, a partner at the pan-European VC firm Expeditions Fund, is the nascent British air defence start-up Cambridge Aerospace, which reached a valuation of $3.4 billion with little but a convincing tech narrative: “They had no battlefield data, no product – just a compelling team and an idea on paper.” It wasn’t all talk: Cambridge Aerospace has begun delivering its Skyhammer air defence missile for taking out Shahed-type drones and cruise missiles. A solid-rocket-motor-powered ballistic missile interceptor, Starhammer, will ship in 2027. In the maritime battlespace, meanwhile, fast-scaling neoprime Kraken Technology Group of Hampshire, UK, has raised $175 million from various VC firms, valuing it at $1 billion, to further develop its uncrewed surface vessel and drone technologies for users including the MoD, NATO and the US Special Operations Command. A solid-rocket-motor-powered ballistic missile interceptor, Starhammer, will ship in 2027. In the maritime battlespace, meanwhile, fast-scaling neoprime Kraken Technology Group of Hampshire, UK, has raised $175 million from various VC firms, valuing it at $1 billion, to further develop its uncrewed surface vessel and drone technologies for users including the MoD, NATO and the US Special Operations Command. Key to it all succeeding, according to Amelia Gould, chief technology officer at Kraken, is a culture that actively nurtures iterative speed – to ensure battlefield systems stay ahead of emerging countermeasures: “Having really quick feedback loops from the warfightersin the field to r for high-consequence innovation,” Gould says. Forging ecosystems The shortening of feedback and iteration cycles, however, means tacticians must increasingly accept imperfect battlefield technologies. “We need to be much more open to minimum viable products, with relatively few safeguards, because, in conflict, staying alive is what matters,” says Hetti Barkworth-Nanton, CEO at Ploughshare, an MoD-owned specialist in turning technology into real-world applications, companies and growth. Ewing agrees: “We’ll definitely see a move away from having so many exquisite platforms, in programmes that take years to define, decades to deliver and decades to wind up, in favour of quicker cycles of technology validation, implementation and adoption.” What kind of spinoffs could emerge from this new way of refining technology? Westwood hopes some powerful answers on clean energy (see box) may emerge. “If we get ourselves really motivated around the fact that we’re boiling the Earth, that could be a real technology driver here,” he says. What makes Westwood so confident of a positive dividend outside the military? An example from history, he says: “We went into world war two with propeller-driven biplanes and came out six years later with jet fighter aircraft. And the subsequent innovation around the jet engine seeded the commercial air transport market that’s been such a huge influence on the way we all live now.” Ukraine’s move has militaries around the world racing to emulate its iterative techniques, which are based on the low-cost technologies behind smartphones and consumer drones: artificial intelligence, mobile connectivity, satellite positioning, cloud storage, digital design systems and 3D printing. “It’s the ability to develop, deploy and iterate these technologies at scale that have been the driver for the drone technology that we see Ukraine using,” says Mark Westwood, director of defence and security at Cranfield University in the UK. Read more about BAE Systems Launchpad at: baesystems.com/launchpad The civilian dividend One of the leading spinoffs from BAE Systems’ Launchpad incubator is start-up Nuclear Turbines of Manchester, UK, which has raised £15 million from four venture funds to begin developing a novel, passively safe 20-megawatt small modular nuclear reactor. The reactor is designed to power data centres and industrial plant. Its novelty is a straightforward one, says CEO Jeremy Owston: instead of driving a vast steam turbine, like a regular reactor, its reactor heats and compresses air to much hotter temperatures to drive a small, commercial gas turbine – greatly simplifying and shrinking the overall power plant. “We’re not building Hinkley Point. We’re targeting the early 2030s to get our reactor up and running and we don’t need tens of billions of pounds to do that. What we’re talking about will need a fraction of the price,” Owston says, adding that he is impressed by the willingness of the VC sector to back such ideas. There are plenty more opportunities worth investing in, says Hetti Barkworth-Nanton at the MoD’s intellectual property spinoff unit, Ploughshare. “Of the billions spent every year in the UK on defence innovation, only a fraction results in IP being spun out. The track record of that innovation reaching civilian markets is weak.” VCs are beginning to notice this opportunity. “There are so many of these funds and they just want to take a bet on something, and that’s great,” says Owston.

item.title: Rewane projects 4.5% growth, urges investors to rethink strategies
item.description: By Onome Onyeme The Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, has projected Nigeria’s economic growth at between 4.3 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, urging investors to rethink traditional investment strategies and embrace emerging opportunities. Speaking at the 23rd edition of the Alpha Morgan Economic Review, held virtually yesterday, Rewane said changing economic realities, technological innovation and evolving business models were reshaping investment decisions globally. “The rules of the past are no longer the rules of the present, definitely not the rules of the future,” he said, urging investors to embrace innovation, research and emerging industries rather than rely on past market performance. Rewane, who examined global economic developments and Nigeria’s investment outlook, said businesses and investors that failed to adapt to changing realities risked losing relevance. He cited the evolution of global businesses, including Apple, as examples of how innovation and leadership could determine corporate fortunes, stressing that past success was no guarantee of future dominance. Rewane observed increasing participation in the capital market, with more companies raising funds through the market rather than relying solely on commercial bank loans. However, he warned of possible property market bubble risks, particularly amid the rapid expansion of construction and property investments in Lagos. Rewane projected that some companies could record revenue growth of between 25 and 40 per cent, driven by capital investment, expansion and increased operations across Africa. He also projected the Naira to trade between N1,500 and N1,600 per dollar in 2027, while anticipating an end to global interest rate increases. He clarified that the projections represented his personal assessment of economic developments. item.title: Five things to expect in 2027
item.description: Things are set to heat up in 2027. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And these impacts will hit as farmers are already struggling with higher prices linked to the war in Iran, and with international aid reduced around the world. Democrats and Trump The Democratic takeover of both chambers of the US Congress in January promises to transform the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, giving his opponents powerful tools to challenge his agenda — but not a free hand to impose their own. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. Perhaps the more immediate impact will come from congressional investigations. Democratic-led committees can subpoena officials and demand documents on alleged corruption, Trump’s family business dealings, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Such scrutiny could trigger lengthy court battles. Democrats could also pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although removing him would require a two-thirds Senate majority — a formidable hurdle. In the Senate, Democrats can block Trump’s cabinet and judicial appointments, including any Supreme Court nominee. But most legislation needs 60 Senate votes to overcome procedural obstruction, and Trump can veto measures that reach his desk. Overriding him requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers. The result could be two years of subpoenas, spending standoffs and confrontation, punctuated by possible deals on shared priorities. item.content:encoded: Things are set to heat up in 2027. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And these impacts will hit as farmers are already struggling with higher prices linked to the war in Iran, and with international aid reduced around the world. Democrats and Trump The Democratic takeover of both chambers of the US Congress in January promises to transform the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, giving his opponents powerful tools to challenge his agenda — but not a free hand to impose their own. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. Perhaps the more immediate impact will come from congressional investigations. Democratic-led committees can subpoena officials and demand documents on alleged corruption, Trump’s family business dealings, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Such scrutiny could trigger lengthy court battles. Democrats could also pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although removing him would require a two-thirds Senate majority — a formidable hurdle. In the Senate, Democrats can block Trump’s cabinet and judicial appointments, including any Supreme Court nominee. But most legislation needs 60 Senate votes to overcome procedural obstruction, and Trump can veto measures that reach his desk. Overriding him requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers. The result could be two years of subpoenas, spending standoffs and confrontation, punctuated by possible deals on shared priorities. French presidential election After 10 years in power, Emmanuel Macron will step down following France’s presidential election, scheduled for April 18 and May 2. Political violence and deepening societal divisions — visible on the streets, in parliament, and across the media — point to a tense election campaign. Key issues on the agenda include pensions, immigration, security concerns, and the situation in Ukraine. Meanwhile, a wave of unrest among high school students will force those vying for the presidency to take a stance on the state of the education system and public services. With far-right candidate Marine Le Pen leading the polls and radical-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon currently projected to advance to the second round, the right and the centre parties are discussing the possibility of a primary. The social-democratic left has held a primary, which was won by Raphael Glucksmann, currently a member of the European parliament. The presidential election has drawn a diverse array of hopefuls, from anti-establishment outsiders and conspiracy theorists to advocates of participatory democracy, former government officials, party dissidents, and even an Olympic judoka. The field is expected to narrow down in the coming months as candidates must secure at least 500 endorsements from elected officials to qualify for the ballot, a hurdle that has historically prevented some hopefuls from entering the race. Another total solar eclipse Following last summer’s total solar eclipse, another is set to take place next summer, on August 2, briefly turning day into night and revealing the Sun’s corona. It will be visible from the far south of Spain, and even more clearly across North Africa and the Middle East. This time, darkness will last for more than six minutes at the centre of the eclipse’s path, promising some spectacular views and images, particularly near the Egyptian Pyramids at midday. A total solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, casting its shadow across a narrow strip of the Earth’s surface. Although the Moon is 400 times smaller than the Sun, it is also 400 times closer to Earth, meaning that the two appear to be exactly the same size in the sky at the moment of the eclipse. Total solar eclipses occur regularly but are less often visible over inhabited land. Women’s World Cup in Brazil After the men’s football World Cup in 2026, it is the women’s turn in 2027 when Brazil hosts a tournament that grows with each new edition. Reigning champions Spain and their star duo Alexia Putellas and Aitana Bonmati will be favourites, but England, who beat the Spanish to claim last year’s European Championship, and four-time winners the USA will also hope to be in the final at the legendary Maracana Stadium on July 25. In men’s club football, Paris Saint-Germain will aim to win a third consecutive Champions League title, a feat not achieved since Real Madrid won three in a row in 2018. After impressive victories in October against Manchester City and Barcelona, Luis Enrique’s team is striking fear into rivals’ hearts and will aim to lift the cup at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on June 5. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: CBN raises BDC’s dollar cash limit to $1m weekly
item.description: Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. item.content:encoded: Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. Authorised dealer banks are also required to report cash disbursed per BDC to the Financial Markets Department (FMD) and Trade and Exchange Department (TED), reconciled with the FXBT, in addition to existing weekly returns. item.title: Uduere: ‘Their sacrifices won’t be in vain’ – Obi, Kwankwaso visit slain NDC members’ families

Meanwhile, Omo-Agege has criticised the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue of the rally, alleging that about 50 officers failed to protect members of the party during the attack. Also, the Obidient Movement condemned Monday’s attack, observing that Nigerians can no longer have confidence in a police force that appears more interested in protecting political interests than protecting citizens, stressing that the police derive their authority from the people. Obi said it was disturbing that some people could resort to killing others simply because they want to occupy political positions, assuring the bereaved families that the sacrifices of the victims would not be in vain. “People cannot sacrifice for this in vain. All the sacrifices will not be in vain. We cannot kill or harm people simply because we want to become political leaders,” he said. Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly representing Ughelli North Constituency I and former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission, was attacked by the assailants while stepping out of his vehicle. He was allegedly shot at close range.
