item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Jimitota Onoyume, Henry Umoru & Egufe Yafugborhi Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, has condemned the killings at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State during Monday’s rally of the party, describing the incident as tragic and unacceptable. Meanwhile, Omo-Agege has criticised the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue of the rally, alleging that about 50 officers failed to protect members of the party during the attack. Also, the Obidient Movement condemned Monday’s attack, observing that Nigerians can no longer have confidence in a police force that appears more interested in protecting political interests than protecting citizens, stressing that the police derive their authority from the people. Obi said it was disturbing that some people could resort to killing others simply because they want to occupy political positions, assuring the bereaved families that the sacrifices of the victims would not be in vain. “People cannot sacrifice for this in vain. All the sacrifices will not be in vain. We cannot kill or harm people simply because we want to become political leaders,” he said. Obi spoke, Tuesday, night during a condolence visit to the family of the late Moses Anaughe, who was shot dead during the attack. Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly representing Ughelli North Constituency I and former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission, was attacked by the assailants while stepping out of his vehicle. He was allegedly shot at close range. At the deceased’s residence in Agbarho, Obi consoled his widow and was seen sharing playful moments with their young son in an effort to comfort the grieving family. He was accompanied by the NDC governorship candidate in Delta State, Deacon Oyovwaiye Chris, and the party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Police came to watch me being executed — Omo-Agege Meanwhile, Omo-Agege expressed disappointment that despite the heavy police presence, the assailants were able to unleash violence on the gathering. He said: “We went to the campaign event with six trucks of policemen deployed to the venue. “We expected protection for everyone at the venue. It never occurred to us that they were merely coming principally to watch me being executed.” Obi, Kwankwaso visit Umukoro’s family The NDC presidential candidate, yesterday, continued his condolence visits alongside his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, with a visit to the family of slain activist in Abraka, Ethiope East Local Government Area of the state, Efemena Umukoro, who was also killed during the party’s campaign rally at Uduere. They were received by the widow, Mrs. Gift Umukoro, and other members of the family. In an emotional moment, Obi carried the couple’s six-month-old baby while the widow wept uncontrollably over the sudden death of her husband. Obi and Kwankwaso offered words of comfort and solidarity to the grieving family. Absent from the visit was Omo-Agege. However, Mrs. Umukoro later confirmed to Vanguard in a telephone conversation that the senator later called her to express his condolences. Earlier, Obi and other party leaders had visited some of the injured victims receiving treatment at a hospital in Warri. Those on the visit include Senator Omo-Agege, Obi’s wife and other leaders of the party. NDC suspends campaigns for seven days Meanwhile, the Media and Publicity Directorate of the party’s governorship campaign office in a statement, yesterday, said: “The NDC Delta State governorship campaign has suspended all its campaign activities for seven days to mourn those killed in the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North. We will announce our next campaign date after the mourning period. “We condemn the deadly attack “We extend our condolences to every bereaved family and stand with those receiving treatment. “Governor Oborevwori owes Deltans a direct answer. What did your administration do to protect lives in Uduere, where did those measures fail, and what will you do now to prevent another attack? We expect him to use the authority of his office to protect every Deltan, regardless of party affiliation. Obidient Movement condemns act In a statement, yesterday by the Director of Media and Communications, Onyeka Dike, the Movement urged Nigerians to take responsibility for their personal security and stop waiting for a police force that he alleges works with the APC to silence opposition voices. “These sustained attacks on NDC supporters in Delta State by APC thugs acting on the orders have continued to receive the tacit endorsement of the Nigeria Police both in the state and at the federal levels. They shot me on the head, Anaughe twice on the chest — Survivor Meanwhile, survivors of the November 23 attack, Chief Evans Ivwurie, Chairman of Omo-Agege’s Campaign Organisation, said he was shot on the head while attempting to establish the safety of the former Deputy Senate President amid the gunfire and stampede that erupted during the NDC, campaign. On the shooting, Ivwurie said: “I personally went to the head of the police to say, how can they be shooting like this, threatening lives? “The policemen told me they were not shooting guns, that they were shooting knockouts. I said, but you can see them brandishing pump actions openly and shooting them. “In the middle of this, APC thugs started throwing stones in the direction of Omo-Agege and our people gathered there. They ended throwing the stones and all of a sudden they started shooting. So, there was serious stampede. The women were running. “Then they started shouting, ‘Where is Omo-Agege? We will kill him. We must kill Omo-Agege. Agege must die today. “Luckily, I saw Omo-Agege’s car moving gently towards me. I quickly ran to his car and got to his door. I wanted to be sure he was safe. “Behold, I just saw one of the attackers. Immediately he saw me at close range, he shot at me on my head. I fell flat to the ground without any energy. I saw that he was trying to shoot me again, so, I tried to get up.” I fell twice, still struggling, as I crept away from that spot. “Then he turned the gun in another direction and I saw him shoot Moses Anaughe. He shot him twice on the chest. “I was in the pool of my blood. I lost so much blood. Blood was gushing from my ear, from my neck, gushing from under my jaw. “Luckily, somebody came to my rescue and they rushed me to the hospital,” he said. Another survivor, Tobore Alex Agbah, who was critically wounded after being shot on the neck, also recounted his ordeal during a visit by Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi. Agbah said: “I’ve five bullets in me. I’m happy to see you, sir. The target was to kill me. There are five bullets in me now,” he told Obi, pointing to his right neck area by his shoulder, left chest and left abdominal and waist regions. Vanguard News The post Uduere: ‘Their sacrifices won’t be in vain’ – Obi, Kwankwaso visit slain NDC members’ families appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NLC, TUC feud: How we brokered peace in Ajaero, Osifo’s rift — Obiajulu
item.description: *lSays some individuals exploited situation to tear labour movement apart By Victor Ahiuma-Young The protracted disagreement between the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport relief agreement with the NLC, which the TUC rejected, threatened to undermine the unity and collective bargaining strength of organised labour. The disagreement escalated into public exchanges and personal attacks between NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, raising concerns that the welfare and interests of Nigerian workers were being overshadowed by the leadership crisis. Worried that the feud could further divide the labour movement and weaken its ability to defend workers’ interests, veteran labour leaders, led by pioneer NLC President, Hassan Sunmonu, intervened and brokered peace between the two leaders. Other prominent figures involved in the reconciliation included Dr Peace Obiajulu, Comrades Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. In this interview, former TUC President, Dr Obiajulu, recounts what triggered the crisis, how it escalated, and how the intervention of the labour elders helped restore cordial relations between the two labour centres. She reveals that poor communication largely fuelled the disagreement, while some individuals exploited the situation, warning that the crisis nearly tore the labour movement apart and ultimately put workers’ interests at risk. What actually led to the disagreement between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress, and how did you get involved in the reconciliation? To start with, I was not even aware that there was a disagreement between the two organisations. I was called by Quadri Olaleye, a former President of TUC. He told me that the President of NLC had asked whether Mrs Obiajulu, whom we fondly call Mummy, had been informed about the meeting. That was when I asked whether there was a problem between TUC and NLC. He said yes. I responded that it was a family matter, just like disagreements between a husband and wife or among children in a family. In all honesty, I do not know who initiated the reconciliation process. I am sure it was the elders. They must have seen what was happening on television and read about it in the newspapers. If I had come across the situation myself, I would equally have reached out to some of the elders to intervene. I would not like to see organised labour become a target of public ridicule. item.content:encoded: *lSays some individuals exploited situation to tear labour movement apart By Victor Ahiuma-Young The protracted disagreement between the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport relief agreement with the NLC, which the TUC rejected, threatened to undermine the unity and collective bargaining strength of organised labour. The disagreement escalated into public exchanges and personal attacks between NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, raising concerns that the welfare and interests of Nigerian workers were being overshadowed by the leadership crisis. Worried that the feud could further divide the labour movement and weaken its ability to defend workers’ interests, veteran labour leaders, led by pioneer NLC President, Hassan Sunmonu, intervened and brokered peace between the two leaders. Other prominent figures involved in the reconciliation included Dr Peace Obiajulu, Comrades Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. In this interview, former TUC President, Dr Obiajulu, recounts what triggered the crisis, how it escalated, and how the intervention of the labour elders helped restore cordial relations between the two labour centres. She reveals that poor communication largely fuelled the disagreement, while some individuals exploited the situation, warning that the crisis nearly tore the labour movement apart and ultimately put workers’ interests at risk. What actually led to the disagreement between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress, and how did you get involved in the reconciliation? To start with, I was not even aware that there was a disagreement between the two organisations. I was called by Quadri Olaleye, a former President of TUC. He told me that the President of NLC had asked whether Mrs Obiajulu, whom we fondly call Mummy, had been informed about the meeting. That was when I asked whether there was a problem between TUC and NLC. He said yes. I responded that it was a family matter, just like disagreements between a husband and wife or among children in a family. In all honesty, I do not know who initiated the reconciliation process. I am sure it was the elders. They must have seen what was happening on television and read about it in the newspapers. If I had come across the situation myself, I would equally have reached out to some of the elders to intervene. I would not like to see organised labour become a target of public ridicule. The moment TUC and NLC begin to quarrel or fall apart, workers are left on their own. Whenever there is a problem within the labour movement, workers are the ones who suffer because nobody will be left to speak effectively on their behalf. How serious had the disagreement become before the elders intervened? If there is a disagreement between NLC and TUC, workers ultimately bear the consequences. Management will take advantage of the division and play one side against the other. Nobody benefits from such a situation. That was why we had to intervene. Eventually, we realised that the problem was largely a misunderstanding arising from a lack of communication. From our perspective, it was more about poor communication and spontaneous reactions than any fundamental disagreement. At the end of the day, the issue was simply that they were not communicating effectively. Some people were also taking advantage of the situation. Can you explain the issues that triggered the disagreement and how they escalated? There were allegations that one party attended a meeting without informing the other. The other party then argued that, based on their existing understanding, both organisations were supposed to be involved in such engagements. Why should one party not be informed before attending a meeting that concerns both organisations? I am sure the leaders themselves might not even have realised that the other party had not been involved. It is possible for someone to attend a meeting and, when asked why another person was absent, simply say that the person did not attend. Nobody might explain that the person was never informed in the first place From our perspective, the underlying problem was a lack of communication. Because they were not communicating, whenever one person made a statement, others would draw the attention of the other party to what was being said about them on television. That would provoke another reaction, and the disagreement would continue to escalate. You mentioned that some people exploited the disagreement. What role did they play in worsening the situation? Some people were taking advantage of the situation. I am sure there were people around them who were not helping matters. However, since that issue was not raised during our discussions, we should not speculate about it. Can I attribute it to the influence of spouses? Sometimes, when two brothers have enjoyed a good relationship for years, marriage can introduce new dynamics into that relationship. If they are not careful, external influences can create disagreements where none should exist. There are certain things one brother might ordinarily overlook, but another person may draw his attention to them and ask why he is tolerating such behaviour. Before long, a minor issue can escalate into a serious disagreement. That is why I keep emphasising the importance of communication. People must be given the opportunity to talk to one another and resolve their differences. What exactly did the elders do to bring the two leaders together and resolve the crisis? We advised them that, going forward, whenever an issue arises, the two leaders should communicate directly with each other. They should not rely entirely on their secretaries or committee chairmen because everybody has their own way of working, and messages can easily be misunderstood or misrepresented. We also shared our experiences from our respective periods in leadership. Things were not always smooth during our time either. There were challenges, but we learnt important lessons. First, you must learn to tolerate certain things. Second, you must maintain a relationship, regardless of the disagreement. If necessary, go directly to the other person’s office and have a conversation. Whatever the problem is, make an effort to reach out. Do not take internal disagreements to the newspapers or television. Communicate with one another and maintain that relationship How did the public exchanges affect the image of organised labour? Those public exchanges were particularly painful to watch. People had already begun questioning the relevance and effectiveness of organised labour under the present administration. Even during the previous administration, there were already comments suggesting that labour was no longer effective and that it had been compromised or bought over. Now, the public disagreements between TUC and NLC were giving critics further grounds to make such allegations. We should not play into their hands. You might think that the people listening to you during a television interview will blame one party or the other. But that is not necessarily what happens. They may end up blaming both organisations. They may ridicule the two leaders and, by extension, the entire labour movement. They will simply conclude that labour has been compromised and that its leaders can be influenced with money. That is not the impression we should allow the public to have of organised labour. Did both parties accept the intervention and agree to put the disagreement behind them? Thankfully, everybody accepted the position of the elders. They understood the issues from our perspective. We were not there to take sides, praise anybody or apportion blame. We were there to examine the bigger picture and protect the collective interest of the labour movement. When we examined the bigger picture, we realise

item.title: Risk of retaining fuel subsidy outweighed political consequences – Idris
item.description: • President misrepresented on electricity supply promise – Onanuga •FG defends power sector reforms, increased revenue to states By Juliet Umeh MINISTER of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the removal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates saved Nigeria from imminent economic collapse. Idris, who spoke at an interactive session with journalists organised by the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council Media and Strategic Communications team in Lagos, Monday, said the President took politically risky decisions in the overriding interest of the country. He maintained that the reforms had improved government revenues at all levels, strengthened the economy and positioned the country for sustainable growth. He said: “When the President took office in May 2023, there were two major policy decisions. One was doing away with this monster called fuel subsidy. The second was ensuring that the multiple exchange rate regimes that we had in this country were also done away with. “Presidents after presidents, everyone knew that fuel subsidy was a big problem and a big drain on the economy of this country. But no one was able to achieve its removal until President Bola Tinubu came. “It was not a convenient decision for Mr President. In fact, it was politically risky for him, for someone who had just won an election, who had just been sworn in and who had another election staring him in the face.” Idris explained that the administration considered the consequences of retaining the subsidy and concluded that delaying the reforms would have been more damaging to the country. “The risk of waiting any longer far outweighed whatever political risk he, as a person, as a president or as a politician, should take. “This created enough fiscal headroom, not just for the Federal Government but also for the sub-nationals. Federal Government has made a lot more money. Sub-nationals have made a lot more money,” he said. Economy on path to recovery The minister also said international financial institutions and rating agencies had acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s economic outlook. He said: “The IMF, the World Bank, everybody is saying, yes, we have some challenges as a nation, but our economy is on the path that will lead us to prosperity. “Our GDP is on the rise. Inflation that was becoming a big problem has been curtailed. Headline inflation, food inflation, all are down.” However, journalists at the meeting raised concerns over persistent insecurity, high petrol prices, inadequate electricity supply, distribution of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and the impact of increased allocations to state governments on citizens’ welfare. He said: “The IMF, the World Bank, everybody is saying, yes, we have some challenges as a nation, but our economy is on the path that will lead us to prosperity. “Our GDP is on the rise. Inflation that was becoming a big problem has been curtailed. Headline inflation, food inflation, all are down.” However, journalists at the meeting raised concerns over persistent insecurity, high petrol prices, inadequate electricity supply, distribution of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and the impact of increased allocations to state governments on citizens’ welfare. Tinubu misrepresented on electricity promise — Onanuga Responding to concerns over electricity supply, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, said Tinubu’s campaign promise on electricity had been misrepresented by the opposition. Onanuga maintained that those circulating the President’s campaign video deliberately omitted a crucial part of his statement. He said: “I think the President has been misrepresented on this power issue. I was there the day he spoke about power. “He said, ‘Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity; you will not pay for estimated bills anymore.’ “Then he went further: ‘A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second time, don’t vote for me.’ “Then he went on and added a caveat. He said, ‘Unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver.’ “If you watch the video, they will never show you the ‘unless’. They yanked it off.” Onanuga identified ageing electricity infrastructure and existing contractual obligations with private electricity operators as some of the challenges confronting the administration. He said the signing of the Electricity Act by Tinubu demonstrated the President’s commitment to decentralising the power sector and empowering states to generate and distribute electricity. “To show you the seriousness of this President, the first thing he did in office was to sign the Electricity Act. “The government is making efforts. The Rural Electrification Agency has been doing a lot to ensure that power goes to people, installing mini-grids in hospitals, tertiary institutions, markets, towns and villages,” he said. Onanuga also said the Presidential Metering Initiative was addressing estimated billing, expressing confidence that Tinubu would fulfil his electricity supply promise by 2031. Meanwhile, Idris pledged sustained engagement with the media ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the administration was willing to receive constructive criticism.” Vanguard News The post Risk of retaining fuel subsidy outweighed political consequences – Idris appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 26 – Eye in the Sky: The Milky Way over Lençóis
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 26 – Eye… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Eye in the Sky: The Milky Way over Lençóis Explanation: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. And there is much to behold in today’s featured image . The Milky Way shines bright in the sky of Brazil , over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park . We can see different parts of the Milky Way as it apparently rotates in the sky every night and throughout the year. This composite image was taken later in the night in July from a latitude of approximately 2º south. It shows some prominent Milky Way features, such as dark dust lanes and colorful nebulas . But does the Galaxy really appear arched like a rainbow in the sky? No, this is an artifact of a picture taken with a wide-angle lens. As the Galaxy was artfully framed by the photographer, it matches the contour of the dark lagoon creating the illusion of a cosmic eye , half in space and half on the ground. Is this eye in the sky looking back at you? Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? item.title: Seeking Refuge on Resolution Island
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Seeking Refuge on Resolution… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the late 1800s, wildlife conservationists in New Zealand were recognizing how predators such as stoats , brought to the country to control other nonnative animal populations, were becoming a threat to native birds. Naturalists at the time surmised that some of the nation’s islands could serve as sanctuaries where endemic species could persist, free from the voracious newcomers. Resolution Island, located in the Fiordland region along the rugged southwest edge of New Zealand’s South Island, was one of the first eyed for this purpose. Conservationist Thomas Henry Potts proposed in 1872 that the island could be a place where “wingless species, and birds of feeble powers of flight, might there find a refuge for some of their representatives.” So began an early systematic effort to protect kiwi, kākāpō , and other native birds on Resolution Island, the largest of the approximately 90 islands in Fiordland National Park . This image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on December 12, 2025, shows the island’s setting amid a landscape of steep-sided valleys carved by glaciers and now inundated by the ocean. The uninhabited island rises from sea level to the summit of Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters (3,507 feet). Its diverse habitats and vegetation communities range from bogs and wetlands near the coast to widespread podocarp forests at middle elevations to tussock grasslands in the subalpine and alpine areas. Offshore, the Taumoana (Five Fingers Peninsula) Marine Reserve protects estuarine and wave-exposed rocky reef habitats at the entrance to Dusky Sound, east of Five Fingers Peninsula. Farther into the sound, Pigeon Island was the onetime home of Richard Henry, who was named caretaker of Resolution Island after it was designated a reserve in 1891. In what some have called a “ landmark effort ,” Henry spent years transporting more than 700 birds, mostly kiwi and kākāpō, by rowboat to Resolution and other would-be island sanctuaries nearby. In 1900, however, people began spotting mustelids on Resolution. It turns out the island is within swimming distance for animals such as stoats. Henry was intent on trapping the interlopers but eventually abandoned the project and moved on to caretaking work on another island. The spirit of his efforts lives on, though. A Department of Conservation program started in 2008 aims to control stoat populations and bolster native species on Resolution. item.title: 10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over
item.description: Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. When you already know the ending, your brain stops racing for answers and begins to notice the machinery holding all those mysteries and themes together. Suddenly, an unreliable narrator's sleight of hand becomes obvious, or a throwaway line in chapter two hits like a freight train in light of later developments .

item.title: 6 Fantasy Books Better Than Harry Potter
item.description: There's no denying that Harry Potter continues to be a phenomenon. After seven bestsellers translated into multiple languages, years of extravagant midnight release parties, eight big-budget films, a stage play, and theme parks, there's still enormous hype for both the upcoming HBO television show and an all-star re-recording of the audiobooks. Clearly, there is something about the boy who lived and his world that draws people in and keeps them captivated. All of this begs one very important question, however: how good are the Harry Potter books, really?

item.title: India’s government ponders cradle to grave AI oversight
item.description: Indian politicians have proposed that AI could take a major role in citizens’ lives, partly through pervasive surveillance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week spelled out his vision for an AI-based app that would collect data about children as they grow and analyze it to determine their aptitude for different types of study or careers. Modi suggested that parents of three-year-old children should enter data about their offspring’s activities and accomplishments into a government-run system that is also accessible to teachers and even a child’s friends. Those records, the PM suggested, will “help identify children's interests and aptitude from an early age and redirect them in the study of their choice in future.” That’s not an entirely creepy idea, because gaining access to India’s top tertiary institutions requires students to pay a hefty fee to sit for entrance exams. Modi pitched recommendations from the AI-powered app as something parents will appreciate as they contemplate whether to fund their offspring’s studies. India’s most populous state, Uttar Pradesh (UP), has proposed to build an “AI Stack” to serve its 240 million-plus residents. A 178-page tender seeks bidders to build a system that uses the state’s Family ID – a unique identifier for each household – to link data held by multiple agencies so it can be put to work in a dozen AI use cases. One of those use cases is a tool for “AI-Enabled Social Media Monitoring and Urban Grievance Detection” that “analyses publicly available social media content including online news channels and connected grievance channels to detect emerging urban issues, citizen complaints, service interruptions, and recurring service gaps.” The government wants that system to autonomously route complaints to relevant agencies, to automate actions like sending crews to patch up damaged roads. Critics have pointed to vague wording in the tender as potentially allowing the UP government to link this system to other agencies – a matter of concern given Indian state and national governments have implemented internet shutdowns to stop protestors from communicating on social media services and messaging apps. Another use case is a knowledge assistant for state police that looks up case histories and other data but can’t use it to assess evidence or provide investigative conclusions. An app for teachers will advise them on how to create custom content to meet students’ needs. Healthcare workers would also get an app to help them make recommendations during patient visits. Citizens get natural language interfaces to a system that offers advice on how to identify and access government services and schemes. UP wants to drive these apps with self-hosted open-weight models, and to use only anonymized datasets. India’s Internet Freedom Foundation worries that the systems described in the tender aren’t explicitly authorized by any legislation, and that the document doesn’t mention important oversight measures for the AI St

item.title: Ridley Scott’s Sci-Fi Thriller Masterpiece Is Officially Being Removed From Netflix
item.description: Ridley Scott is one of those staple filmmakers. The 88-year-old English director has made countless noteworthy films, TV shows, and commercials over the course of his prolific career, dabbling in so many genres that it’s difficult to narrow down the parameters of his work. With the release of this year’s The Dog Stars , Scott has directed 31 feature films. They don’t all share the same characteristics, but broadly, his films are known for huge and immersive sets, battles on an epic scale, and big and heady concepts.

item.title: The sky was once full of stars, kids; then the FCC let Elon Musk launch a million datacenter satellites
item.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. Down on Earth, meanwhile, scientists trying to observe the universe continue to bemoan the obstructions caused by mega-constellations of broadband-beamin
item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. Down on Earth, meanwhile, scientists trying to observe the universe continue to bemoan the obstructions caused by mega-constellations of broadband-beaming satellites. Proposals from across the USA, China, Europe and India currently call for around 100,000 satellites. SpaceX’s proposed million orbiters could run workloads which help us to understand the mysteries of the universe while also making them hard to see from down here. ®

item.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
item.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. Read full article Comments

item.title: Le Pen party leaks: prefect dismissed, Paris deputy prosecutor placed under investigation
item.description: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right party of Marine Le Pen, the National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret, Hugues Moutouh, a former top official at the Interior Ministry, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. And a deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now under administrative inquiry. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight reports.

item.title: Capcom Is Officially Killing Its 'Jurassic World Meets Overwatch' Shooter
item.description: Four years after the game's launch , Capcom is officially shutting down Exoprimal , the company's 5v5 action game about a futuristic dinosaur crisis. Capcom announced Tuesday that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued in September 2027 — meaning that Exoprimal will no longer be playable — and that the game will no longer be sold starting in March 2027.

item.title: New US tariffs: 'Trump lashing out really indiscriminately', expert says
item.description: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dean Baker, Senior Economist at the Centre for Economic and Policy Research, says that "there has to be some mechanism for better coordinating China's involvement in the world trade system and ideally the US, the EU, Canada would have a common front, some clear ground rules that we could agree to, that China could agree to, to be mutually beneficial. It's not a step in that direction, we have President Trump lashing out really indiscriminately. It's very hard to see his approach being very productive".

item.title: Isak and Wirtz on target as resurgent Liverpool sweep aside Club Brugge

On a bitterly cold night in Belgium, Andoni Iraola’s team delivered an accomplished away display to bring Club Brugge’s impressive run to a halt and step closer to automatic qualification from the Champions League group. A week that supposedly represented a test of Liverpool’s credentials has brought rich encouragement before Sunday’s Merseyside derby. item.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
item.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. It's also known as the " Long Night Moon " by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", according to Time and Date , while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees. item.dc:creator: Anthony Wood
item.content:encoded: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. The table below details moonrise timings for a selection of cities spread across the globe for Dec. 23-24: Local moonrise timings for the December 2026 full Cold Moon City Local time New York 3:58 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 London 4:07 p.m. GMT on Dec. 24 Tokyo 4:32 p.m. JST on Dec. 24 Beijing 4:55 p.m. CST on Dec. 24 Sydney 8:36 p.m. AEDT on Dec. 24 Why it's called the Cold Moon The December full moon is often called the Cold Moon in reference to the often freezing temperatures that can descend this time of the year. It's also known as the " Long Night Moon " by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", according to Time and Date , while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees. The December full moon also coincides with the Hindu festival of Datta Jayanti, when followers gather to celebrate the birth of Lord Dattatreya, who embodies the Hindu holy trinity of Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, according to the Government of Maharashtra . The December full moon also rises close to the Christian celebration of Christmas on Dec. 25, when followers celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ. What else to see in the sky around the full moon The Cold Moon will shine in the center of a majestic "Winter Hexagon" of stars bright enough to easily cut through the glare cast by the lunar disk after it rises on Nov. 24. Begin by locating Sirius, the brightest star in our night sky, which rises into the southeastern sky shortly after 8 p.m. local time for viewers in New York. Next, trace an imaginary line to the blue supergiant star Rigel in the nearby constellation Orion, before hopping to the orange glow of Aldebaran , which represents an eye of the great bull depicted in the constellation Taurus. Looking south at midnight on Dec. 23-24 (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva with assets from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio) Next we move to Capella, the jewel of the constellation Auriga, before jumping down to Pollux in the constellation Gemini and nearby Procyon, before closing the loop with Sirius once more. Jupiter and the red light of Mars will shine low in the eastern sky in the hour before midnight, while Saturn will lurk close to the western horizon. Look to the southeast just before dawn to spot Venus appearing as a brilliant "Morning Star", with the red giant Arcturus shining higher in the predawn sky close to the constellation Bootes. Observing tips The December full moon presents a stunning opportunity to photograph the lunar disk as it shines in Earth's sky entirely free from shadow. Be sure to make use of our expert guide to photographing the moon , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography , if you want to upgrade your equipment. Observing tips Use a tripod to keep your camera as steady as possible. Use a remote shutter release or self-timer to prevent camera wobble. A smartphone stargazing app can help you find the exact point of moonrise on your local horizon. A 12–50 mm lens is useful for landscape photography, while at least 400 mm is advised for capturing more detailed views of the lunar surface. The moon can be made to appear particularly large while close to the horizon next to foreground objects, where it may take on an orange-yellow appearance thanks to Rayleigh scattering. A cleaner, more "classic" view can be captured as it soars high overhead. Upcoming full moons Month Full moon name Date and time January Wolf Moon 7:17 a.m. EST (1217 GMT) on Jan. 22, 2027 February Snow Moon 6:23 p.m. EST (2323 GMT) on Feb. 20, 2027 March Worm Moon 6:43 a.m. EST (1043 GMT) on March 22, 2027 These times mark the exact instant of full illumination. Your own moonrise or moonset may be hours earlier or later, depending on your location. For the best viewing plan, use an app such as Stellarium or SkySafari 7 Pro . Editor's Note: If you would like to share your full moon photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s) along with your name, the location and any comments on what it was like to capture the picture to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
item.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. He also called on countries yet to ratify the treaty, particularly African nations, to do so, pledging Nigeria’s commitment to working wi

The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. He also called on countries yet to ratify the treaty, particularly African nations, to do so, pledging Nigeria’s commitment to working with the African Group towards a successful inaugural Conference of the Parties. The ratification marks a strategic step in Nigeria’s efforts to strengthen its position in global ocean governance, protect marine resources and translate the vast economic potential of the blue economy into sustainable national development. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
item.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: “I Don Finally Make My Mama Proud”: Asisat Oshoala Graduates With a Master’s Degree
item.description: Super Falcons striker Asisat Oshoala in her graduation gown and cap at Wembley Stadium after earning her MSc in International Sports Management. Super Falcons striker Asisat Oshoala has added a brand-new title to her name—and this time, it comes with a graduation cap and gown. The Nigerian football star graduated today, Wednesday, 25 November 2026, with a Master of Science (MSc) degree in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sport (GIS) at a ceremony held at Wembley Stadium in London. Sharing photos from the graduation on her Instagram Story, the forward kept her caption short, sweet, and full of charm: “I don finally make my mama proud.” Long before collecting European trophies and continental awards, the Ikorodu-born athlete attended Aunty Ayo International School in Lagos, where she first started playing football before pursuing the sport professionally. Now, alongside her playing career, she holds a postgraduate master’s degree in sports management—equipping herself for leadership roles off the pitch as well as on it. Asisat Oshoala holds two bouquets of flowers while celebrating her Global Institute of Sport graduation at Wembley Stadium. On the field, Oshoala remains one of Africa’s most decorated footballers. Playing primarily as a centre-forward—and occasionally out wide as a winger—the 32-year-old represents Nigeria on the international stage as a key pillar of the Super Falcons, and currently plays club football in the Saudi Women’s Premier League for Al-Hilal, following spells with Arsenal, Liverpool, Dalian Quanjian, FC Barcelona Femení, and Bay FC. Her footballing CV speaks for itself. A six-time CAF African Women’s Footballer of the Year—the first player in history to win the honour six times—Oshoala has won multiple UEFA Women’s Champions League trophies with Barcelona, claimed Liga F and Women’s Super League titles, and represented Nigeria across multiple FIFA Women’s World Cups and Olympic Games. Beyond football, she also runs the Asisat Oshoala Academy and Foundation, which empowers young girls in Nigeria through sports and education. Asisat Oshoala celebrates her Global Institute of Sport graduation at Wembley Stadium alongside her mother and loved ones. Asisat Oshoala celebrates her Master of Science degree in International Sports Management at Wembley Stadium. The post “I Don Finally Make My Mama Proud”: Asisat Oshoala Graduates With a Master’s Degree appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
item.description: Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control. Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year. The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules. Read full article Comments

item.description: Wired, wireless, noise cancelling and budget … here are the headphones to level up your PC and console gaming • The best gaming chairs We talk a lot about graphics in video games; we know how important it is to play on a decent screen so we can see what we’re shooting at … or running away from. But what about sound? Explosions, dialogue, the wheezy breathing of a nearby monster – arguably, audio quality is just as important. Many modern games now support 3D or spatial audio, which lets you detect exactly where a sound is coming from in the game world. In survival horror adventures, you can hear the zombie lurking in the next room, and in popular shooters such as Fortnite and Apex Legends, you can pinpoint the footsteps of approaching enemies. item.title: Campaign rules for influencers? French regulator targets content creators
item.description: Ever since 1965, when the French first got to cast a ballot by universal suffrage for their president, they've valued campaign rules that guarantee ‘equal time’ for candidates. But what does equal time mean when you're closing in on 2027? Last week came a bombshell announcement ahead of next spring’s presidential elections: major online content creators will have to respect the same balanced air time rules as traditional TV and radio broadcasters during the campaign period. Here at FRANCE 24, we’re already testing the stopwatches and combing over the guest list spreadsheets. Should podcasters, YouTubers and influencers be subjected to the same rules as us?

item.title: Meet Funmi Ojo, the University of Ibadan Graduate Who Earned a Perfect 7.0 CGPA
item.description: Doctoral scholar and University of Ibadan alumna Funmi Ojo. There are academic achievements that make you admire a person’s brilliance, and then there are stories that make you think about what determination, self-belief and a second chance can make possible. For Funmi Ojo , earning a perfect CGPA of 7.0/7.0 was about more than getting excellent grades. It was a promise she had made to herself, one shaped by an undergraduate experience in which she felt she had not quite lived up to her own academic potential. This time, she was determined to give herself nothing less than her very best. And she did. Funmi emerged as the Best Graduating Student in the Department of Pharmaceutics and Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Ibadan for the 2024/2025 academic session, completing her MSc in Drug Formulation Science with a perfect 7.0/7.0 CGPA. A Cosmetic Scientist with a B.Pharm from the same university, she is now a doctoral scholar, taking her academic journey into its next chapter. But how do you pursue a perfect score while running a growing business, building a laboratory and making room for the other parts of your life? In this interview with BellaNaija, Funmi talks about the decision to aim for a perfect CGPA from the very beginning, the study systems that helped her get there, and the lessons she learnt about time management, discipline and making the most of every mark. She also shares her thoughts on using AI as a learning tool, tackling difficult courses and knowing when to put everything else aside and focus on the goal. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one. About three weeks into my MSc programme, I had already decided that I wanted a perfect score. I felt I owed it to myself, particularly because I hadn’t achieved the first-class degree I wanted during my undergraduate years. It took getting to 300 level before I became more intentional about my academics, and by then, I realised I was capable of getting excellent grades. I had also seen how much strong academic results could change the trajectory of some of my colleagues, and I didn’t want to feel that I had shortchanged myself. I knew I wanted to get it right this time. Funmi Ojo, Best Graduating Student in the Department of Pharmaceutics and Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Ibadan. Interestingly, my MSc years were also when I took my business most seriously. It was growing rapidly, and I was building my own laboratory, so I had quite a lot to manage alongside my studies. During my undergraduate years, I sometimes blamed my business commitments for my academic performance, but I later realised that I had to learn how to manage my time better. I became more intentional about how I used each hour and stopped making excuses for the things I wanted to achieve. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: Doctoral scholar and University of Ibadan alumna Funmi Ojo. There are academic achievements that make you admire a person’s brilliance, and then there are stories that make you think about what determination, self-belief and a second chance can make possible. For Funmi Ojo , earning a perfect CGPA of 7.0/7.0 was about more than getting excellent grades. It was a promise she had made to herself, one shaped by an undergraduate experience in which she felt she had not quite lived up to her own academic potential. This time, she was determined to give herself nothing less than her very best. And she did. Funmi emerged as the Best Graduating Student in the Department of Pharmaceutics and Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Ibadan for the 2024/2025 academic session, completing her MSc in Drug Formulation Science with a perfect 7.0/7.0 CGPA. A Cosmetic Scientist with a B.Pharm from the same university, she is now a doctoral scholar, taking her academic journey into its next chapter. But how do you pursue a perfect score while running a growing business, building a laboratory and making room for the other parts of your life? In this interview with BellaNaija, Funmi talks about the decision to aim for a perfect CGPA from the very beginning, the study systems that helped her get there, and the lessons she learnt about time management, discipline and making the most of every mark. She also shares her thoughts on using AI as a learning tool, tackling difficult courses and knowing when to put everything else aside and focus on the goal. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one. About three weeks into my MSc programme, I had already decided that I wanted a perfect score. I felt I owed it to myself, particularly because I hadn’t achieved the first-class degree I wanted during my undergraduate years. It took getting to 300 level before I became more intentional about my academics, and by then, I realised I was capable of getting excellent grades. I had also seen how much strong academic results could change the trajectory of some of my colleagues, and I didn’t want to feel that I had shortchanged myself. I knew I wanted to get it right this time. Funmi Ojo, Best Graduating Student in the Department of Pharmaceutics and Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Ibadan. Interestingly, my MSc years were also when I took my business most seriously. It was growing rapidly, and I was building my own laboratory, so I had quite a lot to manage alongside my studies. During my undergraduate years, I sometimes blamed my business commitments for my academic performance, but I later realised that I had to learn how to manage my time better. I became more intentional about how I used each hour and stopped making excuses for the things I wanted to achieve. By the time my responsibilities increased towards the end of the programme, I had already laid the groundwork and knew how to allocate my time. Explain your systems. Beyond “reading hard,” what specific study techniques or daily schedules kept you at the top? I think there are five systems that really made the difference for me. Every mark counts . Don’t wait until examinations before taking your academics seriously. Attendance, laboratory work, continuous assessments, presentations and assignments all contribute to your final grade. It’s often easier to secure 36 out of 40 in your CA than to get 60 out of 60 in an examination. I take every opportunity to earn those marks seriously, especially presentations, which are usually one of my strengths. Those marks can make a real difference. Use AI as a learning tool . AI is one of the biggest advantages students of our generation have. You can upload lecture slides, ask it to explain difficult concepts, provide examples, summarise lengthy materials and generate probable examination questions. Think of it as having a tutorial you can interact with and ask to explain things in a way you understand. Understand that academia is systemic . Knowing something isn’t enough; you also need to retain, recall and communicate it effectively. One of the ways I do this is by teaching others. If you can explain a difficult concept to someone with no background knowledge of the subject, it usually means you understand it yourself. Learn how to answer questions, not just how to read . I think examinations are about 60% knowledge and 40% diction. You need to communicate what you know clearly. I read widely, practise past questions and organise my answers so that my lecturers can follow my thinking. Lock in during examination weeks . A strict daily study routine isn’t always practical when you’re running a business or juggling other responsibilities. So, I maximise the marks available throughout the semester, then give examinations my full attention for those two or three weeks. I temporarily put social activities aside, knowing I can return to them afterwards. Cosmetic Scientist and University of Ibadan graduate Funmi Ojo in a blush pink tweed two-piece outfit. What did you have to sacrifice? Tell us about the social events, personal time, hobbies or even sleep you had to put aside to protect your CGPA. I live a very well-rounded life. I go to the gym, spend time with friends, enjoy my hobbies, read and run a business. So, I wouldn’t necessarily say I sacrificed having a life to achieve my grades. I think it’s more about understanding that certain seasons require you to temporarily put some things aside. During the semester, I make time for my business, friends and other interests while ensuring I secure the 40 marks available outside the final examination. But when examinations come around, I’m completely locked in. For those two or three weeks, I’m not going out or attending social events. If you know me during examination season, you probably cannot call me to do anything else! Once my examinations are over, I go right back to enjoying my life. Funmi Ojo’s University of Ibadan Postgraduate College certificate scroll tube confirming her 2024/2025 PGC Doctoral Scholar award. This is particularly important because I run a business, and work doesn’t simply stop because I have examinations. There are clients, production schedules, employees and other responsibilities to manage. So, I have to be deliberate about scheduling my working hours and creating dedicated time for studying. Ultimately, I don’t think having multiple responsibilities means everything else has to suffer. It’s about understanding your priorities, knowing when each one needs your attention and recognising when it’s time to temporarily pull back. For me, that period is usually the two or three weeks of examinations. How did you handle the toughest courses or departmental hurdles that usually break a student’s GPA? I studied Pharmacy, so there was quite a bit of mathematics and science involved. The funny thing is, I don’t particularly like mathematics. I love chemistry, manufacturing and production, but mathematics? Not so much! I already knew it wasn’t a subject that came naturally to me, so I made sure to give those courses extra attention. My auntie, who is a schoolteacher, always used to tell us that no subject is inherently difficult; sometimes, it’s simply a subject you haven’t read enough or don’t particularly enjoy. I’ve carried that mentality with me because I believe there’s very little you cannot learn if you’re willing to put in the time and effort. Funmi Ojo celebrating her MSc graduation from the University of Ibadan with a 7.0/7.0 CGPA. I think it’s important to identify your difficult courses early rather than spend all your time on subjects you’re already good at. Those challenging courses can make or break your CGPA, so you have to give them the attention they need. For me, that meant revisiting difficult topics, practising and reading until I understood them. I also think the lecturer’s teaching st

item.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
item.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17. Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. A CISA advisory from July describes this technique: The authoring agencies observed Iranian-affiliated APT actors using several foreign-based IP addresses to access internet-facing PLCs manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and potentially other manufactured PLCs [ T0883 ].
